RatFunc.liftOn.code:
RatFunc.liftOn.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [CommRing K] {P : Sort u_2} (x : RatFunc K) (f : K[X] → K[X] → P)
  (H : ∀ {p q p' q' : K[X]}, q ∈ K[X]⁰ → q' ∈ K[X]⁰ → q' * p = q * p' → f p q = f p' q') : P
RatFunc.liftOn.comment:
Non-dependent recursion principle for `RatFunc K`:
To construct a term of `P : Sort*` out of `x : RatFunc K`,
it suffices to provide a constructor `f : Π (p q : K[X]), P`
and a proof that `f p q = f p' q'` for all `p q p' q'` such that `q' * p = q * p'` where
both `q` and `q'` are not zero divisors, stated as `q ∉ K[X]⁰`, `q' ∉ K[X]⁰`.

If considering `K` as an integral domain, this is the same as saying that
we construct a value of `P` for such elements of `RatFunc K` by setting
`liftOn (p / q) f _ = f p q`.

When `[IsDomain K]`, one can use `RatFunc.liftOn'`, which has the stronger requirement
of `∀ {p q a : K[X]} (hq : q ≠ 0) (ha : a ≠ 0), f (a * p) (a * q) = f p q)`.

explanatories.Localization.liftOn: This definition provides a way to define a function on a localization of a commutative monoid by specifying its values for representative pairs in a way that maintains consistency under the equivalence relation used for localization.
explanatories.Localization.r_iff_exists: This theorem establishes that a specific relation between two pairs of elements from a monoid and a submonoid holds if and only if there exists a certain element in the submonoid that satisfies a given equality involving multiplication of these elements.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.mul_cancel_left_coe_nonZeroDivisors: In a commutative ring with non-zero elements, if two products are equal when multiplied by the same non-zero element, then the multiplicands must also be equal.

RatFunc.liftOn.description: The non-dependent recursion principle for rational functions allows the construction of a term in a specified type from a rational function by providing a suitable constructor and a proof of equivalence under certain conditions involving non-zero divisors.

RatFunc.liftOn'.comment:
Non-dependent recursion principle for `RatFunc K`: if `f p q : P` for all `p q`,
such that `f (a * p) (a * q) = f p q`, then we can find a value of `P`
for all elements of `RatFunc K` by setting `lift_on' (p / q) f _ = f p q`.

although many usages of `lift_on'` assume `f p 0 = f 0 1`.

RatFunc.map.fullDefinition: def map [MonoidHomClass F R[X] S[X]] (φ : F) (hφ : R[X]⁰ ≤ S[X]⁰.comap φ) :     RatFunc R →* RatFunc S where   toFun f :=     RatFunc.liftOn f       (fun n d => if h : φ d ∈ S[X]⁰ then ofFractionRing (Localization.mk (φ n) ⟨φ d, h⟩) else 0)       fun {p q p' q'} hq hq' h => by       beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied       rw [dif_pos, dif_pos]       on_goal 1 =>         congr 1 -- Porting note: this was a `rw [ofFractionRing.inj_eq]` which was overkill anyway         rw [Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff]       rotate_left       · exact hφ hq       · exact hφ hq'       refine Localization.r_of_eq ?_       simpa only [map_mul] using congr_arg φ h   map_one' := by     beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied     rw [← ofFractionRing_one, ← Localization.mk_one, liftOn_ofFractionRing_mk, dif_pos]     · simpa using ofFractionRing_one     · simpa using Submonoid.one_mem _   map_mul' x y := by     beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied     cases' x with x; cases' y with y     -- Porting note: added `using Localization.rec` (`Localization.induction_on` didn't work)     induction' x using Localization.rec with p q     · induction' y using Localization.rec with p' q'       · have hq : φ q ∈ S[X]⁰ := hφ q.prop         have hq' : φ q' ∈ S[X]⁰ := hφ q'.prop         have hqq' : φ ↑(q * q') ∈ S[X]⁰ := by simpa using Submonoid.mul_mem _ hq hq'         simp_rw [← ofFractionRing_mul, Localization.mk_mul, liftOn_ofFractionRing_mk, dif_pos hq,           dif_pos hq', dif_pos hqq', ← ofFractionRing_mul, Submonoid.coe_mul, map_mul,           Localization.mk_mul, Submonoid.mk_mul_mk]       · rfl     · rfl

ratfunc.map.fullDefinition: def map [MonoidHomClass F R[X] S[X]] (φ : F) (hφ : R[X]⁰ ≤ S[X]⁰.comap φ) :     RatFunc R →* RatFunc S where   toFun f :=     RatFunc.liftOn f       (fun n d => if h : φ d ∈ S[X]⁰ then ofFractionRing (Localization.mk (φ n) ⟨φ d, h⟩) else 0)       fun {p q p' q'} hq hq' h => by       beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied       rw [dif_pos, dif_pos]       on_goal 1 =>         congr 1 -- Porting note: this was a `rw [ofFractionRing.inj_eq]` which was overkill anyway         rw [Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff]       rotate_left       · exact hφ hq       · exact hφ hq'       refine Localization.r_of_eq ?_       simpa only [map_mul] using congr_arg φ h   map_one' := by     beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied     rw [← ofFractionRing_one, ← Localization.mk_one, liftOn_ofFractionRing_mk, dif_pos]     · simpa using ofFractionRing_one     · simpa using Submonoid.one_mem _   map_mul' x y := by     beta_reduce -- Porting note(#12129): force the function to be applied     cases' x with x; cases' y with y     -- Porting note: added `using Localization.rec` (`Localization.induction_on` didn't work)     induction' x using Localization.rec with p q     · induction' y using Localization.rec with p' q'       · have hq : φ q ∈ S[X]⁰ := hφ q.prop         have hq' : φ q' ∈ S[X]⁰ := hφ q'.prop         have hqq' : φ ↑(q * q') ∈ S[X]⁰ := by simpa using Submonoid.mul_mem _ hq hq'         simp_rw [← ofFractionRing_mul, Localization.mk_mul, liftOn_ofFractionRing_mk, dif_pos hq,           dif_pos hq', dif_pos hqq', ← ofFractionRing_mul, Submonoid.coe_mul, map_mul,           Localization.mk_mul, Submonoid.mk_mul_mk]       · rfl     · rfl

ratfunc.lift_ring_hom.fullDefinition: def liftRingHom (φ : R[X] →+* L) (hφ : R[X]⁰ ≤ L⁰.comap φ) : RatFunc R →+* L :=   { liftMonoidWithZeroHom φ.toMonoidWithZeroHom hφ with     map_add' := fun x y => by       -- Porting note: used to invoke `MonoidWithZeroHom.toFun_eq_coe`       simp only [ZeroHom.toFun_eq_coe, MonoidWithZeroHom.toZeroHom_coe]       cases subsingleton_or_nontrivial R       · rw [Subsingleton.elim (x + y) y, Subsingleton.elim x 0, map_zero, zero_add]       cases' x with x       cases' y with y       -- Porting note: had to add the recursor explicitly below       induction' x using Localization.rec with p q       · induction' y using Localization.rec with p' q'         · rw [← ofFractionRing_add, Localization.add_mk]           simp only [RingHom.toMonoidWithZeroHom_eq_coe,             liftMonoidWithZeroHom_apply_ofFractionRing_mk]           rw [div_add_div, div_eq_div_iff]           · rw [mul_comm _ p, mul_comm _ p', mul_comm _ (φ p'), add_comm]             simp only [map_add, map_mul, Submonoid.coe_mul]           all_goals             try simp only [← map_mul, ← Submonoid.coe_mul]             exact nonZeroDivisors.ne_zero (hφ (SetLike.coe_mem _))         · rfl       · rfl }

RatFunc.liftOn_div.code:
RatFunc.liftOn_div.{u, v} {K : Type u} [CommRing K] [IsDomain K] {P : Sort v} (p q : K[X]) (f : K[X] → K[X] → P)
  (f0 : ∀ (p : K[X]), f p 0 = f 0 1) (H' : ∀ {p q p' q' : K[X]}, q ≠ 0 → q' ≠ 0 → q' * p = q * p' → f p q = f p' q')
  (H : ∀ {p q p' q' : K[X]}, q ∈ K[X]⁰ → q' ∈ K[X]⁰ → q' * p = q * p' → f p q = f p' q' := ⋯) :
  ((algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) p / (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) q).liftOn f H = f p q
RatFunc.liftOn_div.description: This theorem asserts that a certain lifting operation on rational functions, when applied to division, behaves consistently under specified conditions relating to non-zero divisors and the defined function.

  (f : ∀ (p q : K[X]), q ≠ 0 → P ((algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) p / (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) q)) : P x
RatFunc.induction_on.comment:
Induction principle for `RatFunc K`: if `f p q : P (p / q)` for all `p q : K[X]`,
then `P` holds on all elements of `RatFunc K`.

See also `induction_on'`, which is a recursion principle defined in terms of `RatFunc.mk`.

explanatories.Prod.ext_iff: Two pairs are equal if and only if their corresponding first and second elements are equal.
explanatories.gcd_mul_left: This theorem demonstrates that the greatest common divisor of the products of an element with two others equals the normalized value of the first element multiplied by the greatest common divisor of the two latter elements.
explanatories.normalize_apply: This theorem asserts that in a normalization monoid, the normalized version of an element can be expressed as the product of that element and its corresponding unit.
explanatories.Polynomial.coe_normUnit: This theorem states that the coefficient of a polynomial, when normalized, is equal to the normalization of its leading coefficient.
explanatories.CommGroupWithZero.coe_normUnit: This theorem establishes that in a commutative group with zero, the normalized unit of a non-zero element is equal to its multiplicative inverse.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree: This definition assigns the degree of a polynomial as the highest exponent of its variable, with a special notation indicating that the degree of the zero polynomial is undefined.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_gcd_le_right: The degree of the greatest common divisor of two polynomials does not exceed the degree of the non-zero polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_mul: The degree of the product of two polynomials equals the sum of their degrees if the coefficients form a semiring without zero divisors.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_C: This theorem asserts that the degree of a non-zero constant polynomial is zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.C_mul_dvd: This theorem indicates that a polynomial multiplied by a non-zero constant divides another polynomial if and only if the original polynomial also divides that polynomial.
explanatories.GCDMonoid.gcd_dvd_left: This theorem asserts that in a GCD monoid, the greatest common divisor of two elements is a divisor of the first element.
explanatories.GCDMonoid.gcd_dvd_right: This theorem establishes that the greatest common divisor of two elements in a GCD monoid divides the second element.
explanatories.normalize: This definition describes a function that selects a representative from each equivalence class of elements in a normalization monoid by multiplying them by their corresponding unit elements.
explanatories.NormalizationMonoid.normUnit: This definition describes a function that converts each element of a normalization monoid into its corresponding unit element within that monoid.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_zero: This theorem asserts that a polynomial has a leading coefficient of zero if and only if the polynomial itself is the zero polynomial.
explanatories.MonoidWithZeroHom.coe_mk: This theorem establishes that the construction of a zero-preserving monoid homomorphism from a given zero homomorphism is equivalent to the original zero homomorphism itself.
explanatories.ZeroHom.coe_mk: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.dite_false: The theorem establishes that, under a false proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a value based on the negation of that falsehood instead of a value corresponding to that falsehood.
explanatories.Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val: The inverse of a unit element in a division monoid is equal to the inverse of its underlying value.
explanatories.Units.val_mk0: This theorem asserts that the value of an element from the group of units, when constructed from a nonzero element, is equal to that original nonzero element.
explanatories.EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel: Multiplying a number by another and then dividing by a third, provided the first number is non-zero and the third divides the second, results in the same value as dividing the second number by the third.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_div: This theorem asserts that the leading coefficient of the quotient of two polynomials is equal to the division of their leading coefficients, provided the degree of the divisor does not exceed that of the dividend.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul: This theorem establishes that the leading coefficient of the product of two polynomials equals the product of their individual leading coefficients.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_C: This theorem states that the leading coefficient of a non-zero constant polynomial is equal to the constant itself.
explanatories.Polynomial.div_C_mul: This theorem shows that dividing a polynomial by a constant multiplied by another polynomial is equivalent to multiplying the reciprocal of the constant by the quotient of the original polynomial and the other polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.C_mul: This theorem asserts that the constant polynomial of a product of two elements is equal to the product of the constant polynomials of each element.
explanatories.inv_div: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the quotient of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the quotient of the second element by the first.
explanatories.mul_div_assoc: The distribution of multiplication over division holds in a division-inverse monoid, ensuring the equivalence of two expressions involving these operations.
explanatories.inv_inv: This theorem demonstrates that taking the inverse of an element twice in a group retrieves the original element.
explanatories.EuclideanDomain.mul_div_assoc: The result of multiplying an element by another and then dividing by a third is the same as multiplying the first element by the result of dividing the second element by the third, provided the third divides the second.

RatFunc.numDenom.fullDefinition: def numDenom (x : RatFunc K) : K[X] × K[X] :=   x.liftOn'     (fun p q =>       if q = 0 then ⟨0, 1⟩       else         let r := gcd p q         ⟨Polynomial.C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (p / r),           Polynomial.C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (q / r)⟩)   (by       intros p q a hq ha       dsimp       rw [if_neg hq, if_neg (mul_ne_zero ha hq)]       have ha' : a.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 := Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr ha       have hainv : a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ ≠ 0 := inv_ne_zero ha'       simp only [Prod.ext_iff, gcd_mul_left, normalize_apply, Polynomial.coe_normUnit, mul_assoc,         CommGroupWithZero.coe_normUnit _ ha']       have hdeg : (gcd p q).degree ≤ q.degree := degree_gcd_le_right _ hq       have hdeg' : (Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q).degree ≤ q.degree := by         rw [Polynomial.degree_mul, Polynomial.degree_C hainv, zero_add]         exact hdeg       have hdivp : Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q ∣ p :=         (C_mul_dvd hainv).mpr (gcd_dvd_left p q)       have hdivq : Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q ∣ q :=         (C_mul_dvd hainv).mpr (gcd_dvd_right p q)       -- Porting note: added `simp only [...]` and `rw [mul_assoc]`       -- Porting note: note the unfolding of `normalize` and `normUnit`!       simp only [normalize, normUnit, coe_normUnit, leadingCoeff_eq_zero, MonoidWithZeroHom.coe_mk,         ZeroHom.coe_mk, ha, dite_false, Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val, Units.val_mk0]       rw [mul_assoc]       rw [EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel ha hdivp, EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel ha hdivq,         leadingCoeff_div hdeg, leadingCoeff_div hdeg', Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul,         Polynomial.leadingCoeff_C, div_C_mul, div_C_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← Polynomial.C_mul, ←         mul_assoc, ← Polynomial.C_mul]       constructor <;> congr <;>         rw [inv_div, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc, ← mul_assoc, inv_inv, _root_.mul_inv_cancel ha',           one_mul, inv_div])
RatFunc.numDenom.description: This definition provides a way to obtain the numerator and denominator of a rational function over a field, ensuring that the denominator is a monic polynomial.

explanatories.Polynomial.degree: This definition assigns the degree of a polynomial as the highest exponent of its variable, with a special notation indicating that the degree of the zero polynomial is undefined.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_gcd_le_right: The degree of the greatest common divisor of two polynomials does not exceed the degree of the non-zero polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_mul: The degree of the product of two polynomials equals the sum of their degrees if the coefficients form a semiring without zero divisors.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_C: This theorem asserts that the degree of a non-zero constant polynomial is zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.C_mul_dvd: This theorem indicates that a polynomial multiplied by a non-zero constant divides another polynomial if and only if the original polynomial also divides that polynomial.
explanatories.GCDMonoid.gcd_dvd_left: This theorem asserts that in a GCD monoid, the greatest common divisor of two elements is a divisor of the first element.
explanatories.GCDMonoid.gcd_dvd_right: This theorem establishes that the greatest common divisor of two elements in a GCD monoid divides the second element.
explanatories.normalize: This definition describes a function that selects a representative from each equivalence class of elements in a normalization monoid by multiplying them by their corresponding unit elements.
explanatories.NormalizationMonoid.normUnit: This definition describes a function that converts each element of a normalization monoid into its corresponding unit element within that monoid.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_zero: This theorem asserts that a polynomial has a leading coefficient of zero if and only if the polynomial itself is the zero polynomial.
explanatories.MonoidWithZeroHom.coe_mk: This theorem establishes that the construction of a zero-preserving monoid homomorphism from a given zero homomorphism is equivalent to the original zero homomorphism itself.
explanatories.ZeroHom.coe_mk: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.dite_false: The theorem establishes that, under a false proposition, a dependent eliminator produces a value based on the negation of that falsehood instead of a value corresponding to that falsehood.
explanatories.Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val: The inverse of a unit element in a division monoid is equal to the inverse of its underlying value.
explanatories.Units.val_mk0: This theorem asserts that the value of an element from the group of units, when constructed from a nonzero element, is equal to that original nonzero element.
explanatories.EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel: Multiplying a number by another and then dividing by a third, provided the first number is non-zero and the third divides the second, results in the same value as dividing the second number by the third.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_div: This theorem asserts that the leading coefficient of the quotient of two polynomials is equal to the division of their leading coefficients, provided the degree of the divisor does not exceed that of the dividend.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul: This theorem establishes that the leading coefficient of the product of two polynomials equals the product of their individual leading coefficients.
explanatories.Polynomial.leadingCoeff_C: This theorem states that the leading coefficient of a non-zero constant polynomial is equal to the constant itself.
explanatories.Polynomial.div_C_mul: This theorem shows that dividing a polynomial by a constant multiplied by another polynomial is equivalent to multiplying the reciprocal of the constant by the quotient of the original polynomial and the other polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.C_mul: This theorem asserts that the constant polynomial of a product of two elements is equal to the product of the constant polynomials of each element.
explanatories.inv_div: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the quotient of two elements in a division monoid is equal to the quotient of the second element by the first.
explanatories.mul_div_assoc: The distribution of multiplication over division holds in a division-inverse monoid, ensuring the equivalence of two expressions involving these operations.
explanatories.inv_inv: This theorem demonstrates that taking the inverse of an element twice in a group retrieves the original element.
explanatories.EuclideanDomain.mul_div_assoc: The result of multiplying an element by another and then dividing by a third is the same as multiplying the first element by the result of dividing the second element by the third, provided the third divides the second.

ratfunc.num_denom.fullDefinition: def numDenom (x : RatFunc K) : K[X] × K[X] :=   x.liftOn'     (fun p q =>       if q = 0 then ⟨0, 1⟩       else         let r := gcd p q         ⟨Polynomial.C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (p / r),           Polynomial.C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (q / r)⟩)   (by       intros p q a hq ha       dsimp       rw [if_neg hq, if_neg (mul_ne_zero ha hq)]       have ha' : a.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 := Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr ha       have hainv : a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ ≠ 0 := inv_ne_zero ha'       simp only [Prod.ext_iff, gcd_mul_left, normalize_apply, Polynomial.coe_normUnit, mul_assoc,         CommGroupWithZero.coe_normUnit _ ha']       have hdeg : (gcd p q).degree ≤ q.degree := degree_gcd_le_right _ hq       have hdeg' : (Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q).degree ≤ q.degree := by         rw [Polynomial.degree_mul, Polynomial.degree_C hainv, zero_add]         exact hdeg       have hdivp : Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q ∣ p :=         (C_mul_dvd hainv).mpr (gcd_dvd_left p q)       have hdivq : Polynomial.C a.leadingCoeff⁻¹ * gcd p q ∣ q :=         (C_mul_dvd hainv).mpr (gcd_dvd_right p q)       -- Porting note: added `simp only [...]` and `rw [mul_assoc]`       -- Porting note: note the unfolding of `normalize` and `normUnit`!       simp only [normalize, normUnit, coe_normUnit, leadingCoeff_eq_zero, MonoidWithZeroHom.coe_mk,         ZeroHom.coe_mk, ha, dite_false, Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val, Units.val_mk0]       rw [mul_assoc]       rw [EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel ha hdivp, EuclideanDomain.mul_div_mul_cancel ha hdivq,         leadingCoeff_div hdeg, leadingCoeff_div hdeg', Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul,         Polynomial.leadingCoeff_C, div_C_mul, div_C_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← Polynomial.C_mul, ←         mul_assoc, ← Polynomial.C_mul]       constructor <;> congr <;>         rw [inv_div, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc, ← mul_assoc, inv_inv, _root_.mul_inv_cancel ha',           one_mul, inv_div])
ratfunc.num_denom.description: This definition provides a way to obtain the numerator and denominator of a rational function over a field, ensuring that the denominator is a monic polynomial.

RatFunc.numDenom.eq_1.code:
RatFunc.numDenom.eq_1.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] (x : RatFunc K) :
  x.numDenom =
    x.liftOn'
      (fun p q =>
        if q = 0 then (0, 1)
        else
          let r := gcd p q;
          (C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (p / r), C (q / r).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (q / r)))
      ⋯

to the target and a value `x` for the variable in the target.

Fractions are reduced by clearing common denominators before evaluating:
`eval id 1 ((X^2 - 1) / (X - 1)) = eval id 1 (X + 1) = 2`, not `0 / 0 = 0`.

FiniteDimensional.left.code:

  [AddCommGroup A] [Module F K] [Module K A] [Module F A] [IsScalarTower F K A] [Nontrivial A] [FiniteDimensional F A] :
  FiniteDimensional F K
FiniteDimensional.left.comment:
In a tower of field extensions `A / K / F`, if `A / F` is finite, so is `K / F`.

(In fact, it suffices that `A` is a nontrivial ring.)

Note this cannot be an instance as Lean cannot infer `A`.
FiniteDimensional.left.description: The theorem establishes that if a field extension from one field to another is finite, then the extension from an intermediate field to the original field is also finite.

finite_dimensional.left.description: The theorem establishes that if a field extension from one field to another is finite, then the extension from an intermediate field to the original field is also finite.

minpoly.code: minpoly.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) {B : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [Ring B] [Algebra A B] (x : B) : A[X]
minpoly.comment:
Suppose `x : B`, where `B` is an `A`-algebra.

The minimal polynomial `minpoly A x` of `x`
is a monic polynomial with coefficients in `A` of smallest degree that has `x` as its root,
if such exists (`IsIntegral A x`) or zero otherwise.

For example, if `V` is a `𝕜`-vector space for some field `𝕜` and `f : V →ₗ[𝕜] V` then
the minimal polynomial of `f` is `minpoly 𝕜 f`.

explanatories.IsIntegral: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is defined as integral if it can be expressed as a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients from that ring.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_lt_wf: This theorem establishes that the relation of polynomial degrees being less than one another is a well-founded ordering.
explanatories.WellFounded.min: This definition specifies the concept of a minimal element in a nonempty set that is ordered by a well-founded relation.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.

minpoly.fullDefinition: noncomputable def minpoly (x : B) : A[X] :=   if hx : IsIntegral A x then degree_lt_wf.min _ hx else 0
minpoly.description: The minimal polynomial of an element in an algebra is a monic polynomial with coefficients in the base ring that has the smallest degree among those that have the element as a root, if it exists, or zero otherwise.

minpoly.monic.description: The minimal polynomial of an element in an algebra, which is integral, is guaranteed to be a monic polynomial.

Subalgebra.toIntermediateField'.fullDefinition: def Subalgebra.toIntermediateField' (S : Subalgebra K L) (hS : IsField S) : IntermediateField K L :=   S.toIntermediateField fun x hx => by     by_cases hx0 : x = 0     · rw [hx0, inv_zero]       exact S.zero_mem     letI hS' := hS.toField     obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hS.mul_inv_cancel (show (⟨x, hx⟩ : S) ≠ 0 from Subtype.coe_ne_coe.1 hx0)     rw [Subtype.ext_iff, S.coe_mul, S.coe_one, Subtype.coe_mk, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq₀ hx0] at hy     exact hy.symm ▸ y.2

An element `x` of an algebra `K` over a commutative ring `F` is said to be *separable*, if its
minimal polynamial over `K` is separable. Note that the minimal polynomial of any element not
integral over `F` is defined to be `0`, which is not a separable polynomial.

explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.

explanatories.Polynomial.IsSplittingField.adjoin_rootS: The algebra generated by the roots of a polynomial in a splitting field is equal to the entire field containing that splitting field.
explanatories.Polynomial.map: This definition describes a process for transforming a polynomial from one semiring to another using a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.splits_map_iff: The image of a polynomial under a composition of ring homomorphisms splits if and only if the original polynomial splits under the second homomorphism.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq: This theorem establishes that in a scalar tower involving two commutative semirings and an algebra, the algebra map from the first semiring to the algebra is equal to the composition of the algebra maps from the second semiring to the algebra and from the first semiring to the second semiring.
explanatories.Subalgebra.restrictScalars_injective: The process of restricting scalars from one semiring to another is injective, meaning that different subalgebras will map to different subalgebras under this restriction.
explanatories.Polynomial.aroots: This definition describes a multiset of the roots of a polynomial with coefficients in one commutative ring, viewed as a polynomial over a different commutative ring that is also a domain and serves as a T-algebra.
explanatories.Polynomial.map_map: This theorem establishes that applying two successive ring homomorphisms to a polynomial can be simplified by first composing the homomorphisms and then mapping the polynomial with the resulting single homomorphism.
explanatories.Subalgebra.restrictScalars_top: The restriction of scalars from a larger semiring results in the top subalgebra remaining unchanged.
explanatories.eq_top_iff: An element in a partially ordered set is equal to the maximum element if and only if the maximum element is less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin_le_iff: The theorem establishes a condition under which the subalgebra generated by a set of elements is contained within another subalgebra, specifically when the original set is included in that other subalgebra.
explanatories.Algebra.subset_adjoin: The theorem states that any set of elements is contained within the subalgebra generated by that set over a given ring.

Polynomial.IsSplittingField.lift.fullDefinition: def lift [Algebra K F] (f : K[X]) [IsSplittingField K L f]     (hf : Splits (algebraMap K F) f) : L →ₐ[K] F :=   if hf0 : f = 0 then     (Algebra.ofId K F).comp <|       (Algebra.botEquiv K L : (⊥ : Subalgebra K L) →ₐ[K] K).comp <| by         rw [← (splits_iff L f).1 (show f.Splits (RingHom.id K) from hf0.symm ▸ splits_zero _)]         exact Algebra.toTop   else AlgHom.comp (by     rw [← adjoin_rootSet L f]     exact Classical.choice (lift_of_splits _ fun y hy =>       have : aeval y f = 0 := (eval₂_eq_eval_map _).trans <|         (mem_roots <| map_ne_zero hf0).1 (Multiset.mem_toFinset.mp hy)     ⟨IsAlgebraic.isIntegral ⟨f, hf0, this⟩,       splits_of_splits_of_dvd _ hf0 hf <| minpoly.dvd _ _ this⟩)) Algebra.toTop
Polynomial.IsSplittingField.lift.description: The splitting field of a polynomial can be embedded into any field that allows the polynomial to split, preserving the structure of the original field.

polynomial.is_splitting_field.lift.fullDefinition: def lift [Algebra K F] (f : K[X]) [IsSplittingField K L f]     (hf : Splits (algebraMap K F) f) : L →ₐ[K] F :=   if hf0 : f = 0 then     (Algebra.ofId K F).comp <|       (Algebra.botEquiv K L : (⊥ : Subalgebra K L) →ₐ[K] K).comp <| by         rw [← (splits_iff L f).1 (show f.Splits (RingHom.id K) from hf0.symm ▸ splits_zero _)]         exact Algebra.toTop   else AlgHom.comp (by     rw [← adjoin_rootSet L f]     exact Classical.choice (lift_of_splits _ fun y hy =>       have : aeval y f = 0 := (eval₂_eq_eval_map _).trans <|         (mem_roots <| map_ne_zero hf0).1 (Multiset.mem_toFinset.mp hy)     ⟨IsAlgebraic.isIntegral ⟨f, hf0, this⟩,       splits_of_splits_of_dvd _ hf0 hf <| minpoly.dvd _ _ this⟩)) Algebra.toTop

explanatories.Polynomial.SplittingField.splits: This theorem states that a polynomial splits in its splitting field when considered as a morphism from the base field to the splitting field.
explanatories.Polynomial.IsSplittingField.lift: The splitting field of a polynomial can be embedded into any field that allows the polynomial to split, preserving the structure of the original field.
explanatories.Polynomial.SplittingField.lift: This definition provides a way to embed the splitting field of a polynomial into any larger field that also splits the same polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.IsSplittingField.finiteDimens: If a polynomial is a splitting field over a certain field, then the extension formed by adjoining the field with the roots of the polynomial is finite-dimensional over the original field.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofBijective: A bijective algebra homomorphism can be elevated to an algebra equivalence, establishing a strong correspondence between the two algebras.
explanatories.Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_finite: This definition states that a finite-dimensional algebra over a field is considered algebraic over that field.
explanatories.Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHom_bijective₂: This theorem establishes that if there are algebra homomorphisms between two algebras over the same base commutative ring, both mappings are bijective when one algebra is algebraic over that base ring.

polynomial.is_splitting_field.alg_equiv.fullDefinition: def algEquiv (f : K[X]) [h : IsSplittingField K L f] : L ≃ₐ[K] SplittingField f :=   AlgEquiv.ofBijective (lift L f <| splits (SplittingField f) f) <|     have := finiteDimensional L f     ((Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_finite K L).algHom_bijective₂ _ <| lift _ f h.1).1
polynomial.is_splitting_field.alg_equiv.description: This definition establishes that any splitting field for a polynomial is algebraically isomorphic to its associated splitting field structure.

char_dvd_card_solutions_of_sum_lt.comment:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, finitary version.
Let `(f i)` be a finite family of multivariate polynomials
in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`) over a finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the sum of the total degrees of the `f i` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of common solutions of the `f i` is divisible by `p`.

The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, unary version.
Let `f` be a multivariate polynomial in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`)
over a finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the total degree of `f` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.

char_dvd_card_solutions_of_add_lt.comment:
The **Chevalley–Warning theorem**, binary version.
Let `f₁`, `f₂` be two multivariate polynomials in finitely many variables (`X s`, `s : σ`) over a
finite field of characteristic `p`.
Assume that the sum of the total degrees of `f₁` and `f₂` is less than the cardinality of `σ`.
Then the number of common solutions of the `f₁` and `f₂` is divisible by `p`.

IntermediateField.adjoin.description: The adjoin operation extends a field by incorporating a specified set of elements from a larger field.

intermediate_field.finite_dimensional_su.fullDefinition: instance finiteDimensional_iSup_of_finite [h : Finite ι] [∀ i, FiniteDimensional K (t i)] :     FiniteDimensional K (⨆ i, t i : IntermediateField K L) := by   rw [← iSup_univ]   let P : Set ι → Prop := fun s => FiniteDimensional K (⨆ i ∈ s, t i : IntermediateField K L)   change P Set.univ   apply Set.Finite.induction_on   all_goals dsimp only [P]   · exact Set.finite_univ   · rw [iSup_emptyset]     exact (botEquiv K L).symm.toLinearEquiv.finiteDimensional   · intro _ s _ _ hs     rw [iSup_insert]     exact IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_sup _ _

IntermediateField.restrictScalars_adjoin.code:
IntermediateField.restrictScalars_adjoin_of_algEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] {E : Type u_2}
  [Field E] [Algebra F E] {L : Type u_3} {L' : Type u_4} [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra F L] [Algebra L E] [Algebra F L']
  [Algebra L' E] [IsScalarTower F L E] [IsScalarTower F L' E] (i : L ≃ₐ[F] L')
  (hi : ⇑(algebraMap L E) = ⇑(algebraMap L' E) ∘ ⇑i) (S : Set E) :
  restrictScalars F (adjoin L S) = restrictScalars F (adjoin L' S)
IntermediateField.restrictScalars_adjoin.comment:
If `E / L / F` and `E / L' / F` are two field extension towers, `L ≃ₐ[F] L'` is an isomorphism
compatible with `E / L` and `E / L'`, then for any subset `S` of `E`, `L(S)` and `L'(S)` are
equal as intermediate fields of `E / F`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Subalgebra.restrictScalars: A subalgebra of a larger algebra can be restricted to a smaller base field, allowing it to be viewed as a subalgebra with respect to that field while preserving the algebraic structure.

IntermediateField.restrictScalars_adjoin.description: The theorem states that when two field extension towers share an isomorphism that is compatible with a larger field, the fields generated by adjoining a set of elements from the larger field are equal when restricted to the base field.

  [Algebra K L] (E1 E2 : IntermediateField K L) (halg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic K ↥E1 ∨ Algebra.IsAlgebraic K ↥E2) :
  (E1 ⊔ E2).toSubalgebra = E1.toSubalgebra ⊔ E2.toSubalgebra
IntermediateField.sup_toSubalgebra_of_is.comment:
The compositum of two intermediate fields is equal to the compositum of them
as subalgebras, if one of them is algebraic over the base field.

explanatories.IntermediateField.toSubalgebra: The definition converts an intermediate field into a subalgebra over a specified field.
explanatories.IsAlgebraic: This definition describes an element in an R-algebra as being algebraic over R if it satisfies a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients from R.

IntermediateField.sup_toSubalgebra_of_is.description: The theorem states that the union of two intermediate fields is equivalent to the union of their respective subalgebras if at least one of the intermediate fields is algebraic over the base field.

IntermediateField.adjoin_toSubalgebra_of.code:
IntermediateField.adjoin_toSubalgebra_of_isAlgebraic.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] (E : Type u_2) [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (L : IntermediateField F K)
  (halg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E ∨ Algebra.IsAlgebraic F ↥L) : (adjoin E ↑L).toSubalgebra = Algebra.adjoin E ↑L
IntermediateField.adjoin_toSubalgebra_of.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, `L` is an intermediate field of `K / F`, such that
either `E / F` or `L / F` is algebraic, then `E(L) = E[L]`.

explanatories.IntermediateField.toSubalgebra: The definition converts an intermediate field into a subalgebra over a specified field.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.IsAlgebraic: This definition describes an element in an R-algebra as being algebraic over R if it satisfies a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients from R.

IntermediateField.adjoin_toSubalgebra_of.description: The theorem states that if either the extension from one field to another is algebraic or an intermediate field is algebraic, then the subalgebra generated by adjoining elements from the extension to the intermediate field is equivalent to the algebra generated by those same elements.

IntermediateField.adjoin_rank_le_of_isAl.code:
IntermediateField.adjoin_rank_le_of_isAlgebraic.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] (E : Type u_2) [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (L : IntermediateField F K)
  (halg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E ∨ Algebra.IsAlgebraic F ↥L) : Module.rank E ↥(adjoin E ↑L) ≤ Module.rank F ↥L
IntermediateField.adjoin_rank_le_of_isAl.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, `L` is an intermediate field of `K / F`, such that
either `E / F` or `L / F` is algebraic, then `[E(L) : E] ≤ [L : F]`. A corollary of
`Subalgebra.adjoin_rank_le` since in this case `E(L) = E[L]`.

explanatories.IsAlgebraic: This definition describes an element in an R-algebra as being algebraic over R if it satisfies a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients from R.
explanatories.Module.rank: This defines the rank of a module as the supremum of the cardinalities of its linearly independent subsets, aligning with the dimension of a vector space for free modules over certain types of rings.

IntermediateField.adjoin_rank_le_of_isAl.description: The rank of the extension of a field that adjoins an intermediate field is less than or equal to the rank of the original field extension provided that at least one of two algebraic conditions is satisfied.

IntermediateField.adjoinRootEquivAdjoin.fullDefinition: noncomputable def adjoinRootEquivAdjoin (h : IsIntegral F α) :     AdjoinRoot (minpoly F α) ≃ₐ[F] F⟮α⟯ :=   AlgEquiv.ofBijective     (AdjoinRoot.liftHom (minpoly F α) (AdjoinSimple.gen F α) (aeval_gen_minpoly F α))     (by       set f := AdjoinRoot.lift _ _ (aeval_gen_minpoly F α : _)       haveI := Fact.mk (minpoly.irreducible h)       constructor       · exact RingHom.injective f       · suffices F⟮α⟯.toSubfield ≤ RingHom.fieldRange (F⟮α⟯.toSubfield.subtype.comp f) by           intro x           obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := this (Subtype.mem x)           exact ⟨y, Subtype.ext hy⟩         refine Subfield.closure_le.mpr (Set.union_subset (fun x hx => ?_) ?_)         · obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hx           refine ⟨y, ?_⟩           -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644           erw [RingHom.comp_apply, AdjoinRoot.lift_of (aeval_gen_minpoly F α)]           exact hy         · refine Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr ⟨AdjoinRoot.root (minpoly F α), ?_⟩           -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644           erw [RingHom.comp_apply, AdjoinRoot.lift_root (aeval_gen_minpoly F α)]           rfl)

AdjoinRoot.algEquivOfAssociated.fullDefinition: noncomputable def algEquivOfAssociated {p q : K[X]} (hp : p ≠ 0) (hpq : Associated p q) :     AdjoinRoot p ≃ₐ[K] AdjoinRoot q :=   ofAlgHom (liftHom p (root q) (by simp only [aeval_eq, mk_eq_zero, hpq.symm.dvd] ))     (liftHom q (root p) (by simp only [aeval_eq, mk_eq_zero, hpq.dvd]))     ( PowerBasis.algHom_ext (powerBasis (hpq.ne_zero_iff.mp hp))         (by rw [powerBasis_gen (hpq.ne_zero_iff.mp hp), AlgHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,           liftHom_root, liftHom_root, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq]))     (PowerBasis.algHom_ext (powerBasis hp)       (by rw [powerBasis_gen hp, AlgHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, liftHom_root, liftHom_root,           AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq]))

IntermediateField.normal_iSup.fullDefinition: instance normal_iSup {ι : Type*} (t : ι → IntermediateField F K) [h : ∀ i, Normal F (t i)] :     Normal F (⨆ i, t i : IntermediateField F K) := by   refine { toIsAlgebraic := isAlgebraic_iSup fun i => (h i).1, splits' := fun x => ?_ }   obtain ⟨s, hx⟩ := exists_finset_of_mem_supr'' (fun i => (h i).1) x.2   let E : IntermediateField F K := ⨆ i ∈ s, adjoin F ((minpoly F (i.2 : _)).rootSet K)   have hF : Normal F E := by     haveI : IsSplittingField F E (∏ i ∈ s, minpoly F i.snd) := by       refine isSplittingField_iSup ?_ fun i _ => adjoin_rootSet_isSplittingField ?_       · exact Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun i _ => minpoly.ne_zero ((h i.1).isIntegral i.2)       · exact Polynomial.splits_comp_of_splits _ (algebraMap (t i.1) K) ((h i.1).splits i.2)     apply Normal.of_isSplittingField (∏ i ∈ s, minpoly F i.2)   have hE : E ≤ ⨆ i, t i := by     refine iSup_le fun i => iSup_le fun _ => le_iSup_of_le i.1 ?_     rw [adjoin_le_iff, ← image_rootSet ((h i.1).splits i.2) (t i.1).val]     exact fun _ ⟨a, _, h⟩ => h ▸ a.2   have := hF.splits ⟨x, hx⟩   rw [minpoly_eq, Subtype.coe_mk, ← minpoly_eq] at this   exact Polynomial.splits_comp_of_splits _ (inclusion hE).toRingHom this

explanatories.IsIntegral.tower_top: If an element is integral over a commutative ring in an algebra tower, then it is also integral over the intermediate algebra.

AlgHom.restrictNormalAux.fullDefinition: def AlgHom.restrictNormalAux [h : Normal F E] :     (toAlgHom F E K₁).range →ₐ[F] (toAlgHom F E K₂).range where   toFun x :=     ⟨ϕ x, by       suffices (toAlgHom F E K₁).range.map ϕ ≤ _ by exact this ⟨x, Subtype.mem x, rfl⟩       rintro x ⟨y, ⟨z, hy⟩, hx⟩       rw [← hx, ← hy]       apply minpoly.mem_range_of_degree_eq_one E       refine         Or.resolve_left (h.splits z).def (minpoly.ne_zero (h.isIntegral z)) (minpoly.irreducible ?_)           (minpoly.dvd E _ (by simp [aeval_algHom_apply]))       simp only [AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, AlgHom.coe_toRingHom]       suffices IsIntegral F _ by exact this.tower_top       exact ((h.isIntegral z).map <| toAlgHom F E K₁).map ϕ⟩   map_zero' := Subtype.ext (map_zero _)   map_one' := Subtype.ext (map_one _)   map_add' x y := Subtype.ext <| by simp   map_mul' x y := Subtype.ext <| by simp   commutes' x := Subtype.ext (ϕ.commutes x)
AlgHom.restrictNormalAux.description: This definition describes a method for restricting an algebra homomorphism from one field extension to the image of a normal subfield to another field extension while preserving algebraic structure.

explanatories.AlgHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two algebra homomorphisms are identical if they yield the same output for every element in the source algebra.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.restrictNormal_commutes: This theorem shows that when restricting an algebraic equivalence between two field extensions, the algebra map from the normal extension to the second field is consistent with applying the equivalence after the algebra map from the normal extension to the first field.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ext: This theorem establishes that if two algebra equivalence functions yield the same result for all elements in the first algebra, then they are indeed the same function.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.toAlgHom_eq_coe: This theorem asserts that an algebra equivalence can be identified with its corresponding algebra homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.coe_ofBijective: The theorem states that if a function between two algebras is bijective, then the algebra equivalence constructed from this function agrees with the original function when evaluated.
explanatories.NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective: This theorem establishes that the algebra map from a commutative ring to a ring is injective when the target ring has no zero divisors under scalar multiplication.

normal.alg_hom_equiv_aut.fullDefinition: def Normal.algHomEquivAut [Normal F E] : (E →ₐ[F] K₁) ≃ E ≃ₐ[F] E where   toFun σ := AlgHom.restrictNormal' σ E   invFun σ := (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F E K₁).comp σ.toAlgHom   left_inv σ := by     ext     simp [AlgHom.restrictNormal']   right_inv σ := by     ext     simp only [AlgHom.restrictNormal', AlgEquiv.toAlgHom_eq_coe, AlgEquiv.coe_ofBijective]     apply NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective E K₁     rw [AlgHom.restrictNormal_commutes]     simp
normal.alg_hom_equiv_aut.description: This definition establishes a correspondence between algebra homomorphisms from a normal field extension to a base field and algebra isomorphisms of the normal field itself.

  [Algebra F K₁] [Algebra F K₂] (ϕ : K₁ →ₐ[F] K₂) (E : Type u_6) [Field E] [Algebra F E] [Algebra K₁ E] [Algebra K₂ E]
  [IsScalarTower F K₁ E] [IsScalarTower F K₂ E] [h : Normal F E] : E →ₐ[F] E
AlgHom.liftNormal.comment:
If `E/Kᵢ/F` are towers of fields with `E/F` normal then we can lift
an algebra homomorphism `ϕ : K₁ →ₐ[F] K₂` to `ϕ.liftNormal E : E →ₐ[F] E`.

explanatories.Normal.out: This theorem indicates that if a field extension is normal, then every element of the extension is integral over the base field and its minimal polynomial splits over that field.
explanatories.minpoly.ne_zero: The minimal polynomial of an integral element in an algebra over a nontrivial commutative ring is guaranteed to be nonzero.
explanatories.Polynomial.IsRoot.def: This theorem states that a number is a root of a polynomial if and only if the evaluation of that polynomial at that number equals zero.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq: This theorem establishes that in a scalar tower involving two commutative semirings and an algebra, the algebra map from the first semiring to the algebra is equal to the composition of the algebra maps from the second semiring to the algebra and from the first semiring to the second semiring.
explanatories.IsIntegral.tower_top: If an element is integral over a commutative ring in an algebra tower, then it is also integral over the intermediate algebra.
explanatories.Polynomial.splits_of_splits_of_dvd: If a polynomial splits under a ring homomorphism and divides another non-zero polynomial, then the dividing polynomial also splits under that homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.map_ne_zero: This theorem states that if a polynomial is non-zero and a ring homomorphism is applied to it, then the resulting polynomial after mapping will also be non-zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.splits_map_iff: The image of a polynomial under a composition of ring homomorphisms splits if and only if the original polynomial splits under the second homomorphism.
explanatories.minpoly.dvd_map_of_isScalarTower: The minimal polynomial of an element in a scalar tower divides the image of its minimal polynomial mapped through the algebra homomorphism from the base ring to the intermediate field.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.toAlgHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebraic equivalence between two algebras over a commutative semiring as an algebra homomorphism between them.
explanatories.RingHom.toAlgebra: This definition provides a way to construct an algebra over a commutative semiring from a ring homomorphism to another commutative semiring.
explanatories.AlgHom.restrictScalars: The restriction of scalars allows for the construction of a homomorphism from an algebra over a base commutative semiring to an algebra over a smaller base semiring induced by the original structure.
explanatories.IntermediateField.restrictScalars: This definition describes how to interpret an intermediate field as a field base extension in a tower of field extensions involving multiple fields.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.toAlgHom: This definition states that in a scalar tower, there exists a canonical algebra homomorphism from the middle element to the top element that respects the structure of the bottom element.
explanatories.Polynomial.Splits.def: If a polynomial is said to split over a field, then it is either zero or every irreducible factor of its image has a degree of one.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.Nonempty.some: A nonempty type guarantees the existence of an element that can be extracted from it.
explanatories.IntermediateField.nonempty_algHom_of_adj: This theorem establishes the existence of a non-empty set of algebra homomorphisms from one field extension to another if every element in a given set is integral and their corresponding minimal polynomials split in the target field.
explanatories.IntermediateField.adjoin_univ: The theorem states that the algebra generated by a field over the entire set of elements in an algebra is equal to the largest possible intermediate field.

AlgHom.liftNormal.fullDefinition: noncomputable def AlgHom.liftNormal [h : Normal F E] : E →ₐ[F] E :=   @AlgHom.restrictScalars F K₁ E E _ _ _ _ _ _       ((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F K₂ E).comp ϕ).toRingHom.toAlgebra _ _ _ _ <|     Nonempty.some <|       @IntermediateField.nonempty_algHom_of_adjoin_splits _ _ _ _ _ _ _         ((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F K₂ E).comp ϕ).toRingHom.toAlgebra _         (fun x _ ↦ ⟨(h.out x).1.tower_top,           splits_of_splits_of_dvd _ (map_ne_zero (minpoly.ne_zero (h.out x).1))             -- Porting note: had to override typeclass inference below using `(_)`             (by rw [splits_map_iff, ← @IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq _ _ _ _ _ _ (_) (_) (_)]                 exact (h.out x).2)             (minpoly.dvd_map_of_isScalarTower F K₁ x)⟩)         (IntermediateField.adjoin_univ _ _)
AlgHom.liftNormal.description: This definition describes a method to lift an algebra homomorphism between two fields through a normal extension in a tower of fields, allowing the homomorphism to be extended to the larger field.

PerfectClosure.instAddCommGroup.fullDefinition: instance instAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup (PerfectClosure K p) :=   { (inferInstance : Add (PerfectClosure K p)),     (inferInstance : Neg (PerfectClosure K p)) with     add_assoc := fun e f g =>       Quot.inductionOn e fun ⟨m, x⟩ =>         Quot.inductionOn f fun ⟨n, y⟩ =>           Quot.inductionOn g fun ⟨s, z⟩ => by             simp only [quot_mk_eq_mk, mk_add_mk] -- Porting note: added this line             apply congr_arg (Quot.mk _)             simp only [iterate_map_add, ← iterate_add_apply, add_assoc, add_comm s _]     zero := 0     zero_add := fun e =>       Quot.inductionOn e fun ⟨n, x⟩ =>         congr_arg (Quot.mk _) <| by           simp only [iterate_map_zero, iterate_zero_apply, zero_add]     add_zero := fun e =>       Quot.inductionOn e fun ⟨n, x⟩ =>         congr_arg (Quot.mk _) <| by           simp only [iterate_map_zero, iterate_zero_apply, add_zero]     sub_eq_add_neg := fun a b => rfl     add_left_neg := fun e =>       Quot.inductionOn e fun ⟨n, x⟩ => by         simp only [quot_mk_eq_mk, neg_mk, mk_add_mk, iterate_map_neg, add_left_neg, mk_zero]     add_comm := fun e f =>       Quot.inductionOn e fun ⟨m, x⟩ =>         Quot.inductionOn f fun ⟨n, y⟩ => congr_arg (Quot.mk _) <| by simp only [add_comm]     nsmul := nsmulRec     zsmul := zsmulRec }

PerfectClosure.lift.fullDefinition: noncomputable def lift (L : Type v) [CommSemiring L] [CharP L p] [PerfectRing L p] :     (K →+* L) ≃ (PerfectClosure K p →+* L) where   toFun f :=     { toFun := by         refine fun e => liftOn e (fun x => (frobeniusEquiv L p).symm^[x.1] (f x.2)) ?_         rintro - - ⟨n, x⟩         simp [f.map_frobenius]       map_one' := f.map_one       map_zero' := f.map_zero       map_mul' := by         rintro ⟨n, x⟩ ⟨m, y⟩         simp only [quot_mk_eq_mk, liftOn_mk, f.map_iterate_frobenius, mk_mul_mk, map_mul,           iterate_map_mul]         have := LeftInverse.iterate (frobeniusEquiv_symm_apply_frobenius L p)         rw [iterate_add_apply, this _ _, add_comm, iterate_add_apply, this _ _]       map_add' := by         rintro ⟨n, x⟩ ⟨m, y⟩         simp only [quot_mk_eq_mk, liftOn_mk, f.map_iterate_frobenius, mk_add_mk, map_add,           iterate_map_add]         have := LeftInverse.iterate (frobeniusEquiv_symm_apply_frobenius L p)         rw [iterate_add_apply, this _ _, add_comm n, iterate_add_apply, this _ _] }   invFun f := f.comp (of K p)   left_inv f := by ext x; rfl   right_inv f := by     ext ⟨n, x⟩     simp only [quot_mk_eq_mk, RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.coe_mk, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk,       liftOn_mk]     apply (injective_frobenius L p).iterate n     rw [← f.map_iterate_frobenius, iterate_frobenius_mk,       RightInverse.iterate (frobenius_apply_frobeniusEquiv_symm L p) n]

explanatories.NoZeroSMulDivisors.of_algebraMap_injecti: This theorem establishes that if the algebra map from a commutative semiring to another semiring is injective and the latter has no zero divisors, then a product of elements in the first semiring is zero if and only if at least one of those elements is zero.

explanatories.RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra: This theorem establishes that the algebra map from one commutative semiring to another coincides with a given ring homomorphism.

IsAlgClosure.equivOfEquivAux.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equivOfEquivAux (hSR : S ≃+* R) :     { e : L ≃+* M // e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap S L) = (algebraMap R M).comp hSR.toRingHom } := by   letI : Algebra R S := RingHom.toAlgebra hSR.symm.toRingHom   letI : Algebra S R := RingHom.toAlgebra hSR.toRingHom   letI : IsDomain R := (NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R M).isDomain _   letI : IsDomain S := (NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective S L).isDomain _   letI : Algebra R L := RingHom.toAlgebra ((algebraMap S L).comp (algebraMap R S))   haveI : IsScalarTower R S L := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl   haveI : IsScalarTower S R L :=     IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (by simp [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra])   haveI : NoZeroSMulDivisors R S := NoZeroSMulDivisors.of_algebraMap_injective hSR.symm.injective   have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic R L := (IsAlgClosure.algebraic.tower_top_of_injective     (show Function.Injective (algebraMap S R) from hSR.injective))   refine     ⟨equivOfAlgebraic' R S L M, ?_⟩   ext x   simp only [RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe, Function.comp_apply, RingHom.coe_comp,     AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom]   conv_lhs => rw [← hSR.symm_apply_apply x]   show equivOfAlgebraic' R S L M (algebraMap R L (hSR x)) = _   rw [AlgEquiv.commutes]
IsAlgClosure.equivOfEquivAux.description: This definition introduces a type of equivalence between two algebraic structures such that the composition of ring homomorphisms preserves the algebraic map properties between them.

  [Field K] [Field A] [Algebra F K] [Algebra F A] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K] [IsAlgClosed A] (x : K) :
  (Set.range fun ψ => ψ x) = (minpoly F x).rootSet A
Algebra.IsAlgebraic.range_eval_eq_rootSe.comment:
Let `A` be an algebraically closed field and let `x ∈ K`, with `K/F` an algebraic extension
of fields. Then the images of `x` by the `F`-algebra morphisms from `K` to `A` are exactly
the roots in `A` of the minimal polynomial of `x` over `F`.

IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSpl.comment:
All `F`-embeddings of a field `K` into another field `A` factor through any intermediate
field of `A/F` in which the minimal polynomial of elements of `K` splits.

explanatories.Polynomial.Splits: A polynomial is said to split if it is either zero or all of its irreducible factors have a degree of one.
explanatories.Polynomial.map: This definition describes a process for transforming a polynomial from one semiring to another using a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.IsRoot.def: This theorem states that a number is a root of a polynomial if and only if the evaluation of that polynomial at that number equals zero.
explanatories.RingHom.injective: This theorem asserts that a ring homomorphism from a division ring to a non-trivial semiring is injective, meaning it preserves distinctness of elements.
explanatories.RingEquiv.injective: This theorem asserts that a ring isomorphism is an injective function.
explanatories.Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral: If an algebra over a commutative ring is integral, then every element of that algebra is also integral over the commutative ring.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Function.Injective.comp: This theorem does not contain any information or statement to interpret.
explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgHom.codRestrict: This definition allows for the restriction of an algebra homomorphism's codomain to a specified subalgebra.
explanatories.IsIntegral.map: If an element of a ring is integral over a commutative ring, then its image under a ring homomorphism into another algebra is also integral over the same commutative ring.
explanatories.minpoly.algHom_eq: The minimal polynomial of an element in an algebra remains unchanged under injective algebra homomorphisms.

IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSpl.fullDefinition: def IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSplits (L : IntermediateField F A)     (hL : ∀ x : K, (minpoly F x).Splits (algebraMap F L)) :     (K →ₐ[F] L) ≃ (K →ₐ[F] A) where   toFun := L.val.comp   invFun f := f.codRestrict _ fun x ↦     ((Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral x).map f).mem_intermediateField_of_minpoly_splits <| by       rw [minpoly.algHom_eq f f.injective]; exact hL x   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := by rfl
IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSpl.description: This definition establishes a structure-preserving bijection between the sets of F-algebra homomorphisms from a field K to an intermediate field L and from K to another field A, under the condition that the minimal polynomial of elements in K splits in L.

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHomEquivAlgHomOfS.code:

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHomEquivAlgHomOfS.comment:
All `F`-embeddings of a field `K` into another field `A` factor through any subextension
of `A/F` in which the minimal polynomial of elements of `K` splits.

explanatories.Polynomial.Splits: A polynomial is said to split if it is either zero or all of its irreducible factors have a degree of one.
explanatories.Polynomial.IsRoot.def: This theorem states that a number is a root of a polynomial if and only if the evaluation of that polynomial at that number equals zero.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.toAlgHom: This definition states that in a scalar tower, there exists a canonical algebra homomorphism from the middle element to the top element that respects the structure of the bottom element.
explanatories.Algebra.IsAlgebraic.trans: This theorem asserts that an algebraic algebra over an algebraic field extension is also algebraic over the original field.
explanatories.IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSpl: This definition establishes a structure-preserving bijection between the sets of F-algebra homomorphisms from a field K to an intermediate field L and from K to another field A, under the condition that the minimal polynomial of elements in K splits in L.

explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField: An algebra homomorphism between fields can be restricted to an algebra isomorphism between the field and the subalgebra formed by its range.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.AlgHom.fieldRange: The range of an algebra homomorphism between two fields is defined as an intermediate field over the base field.
explanatories.Polynomial.splits_of_algHom: If a polynomial splits under a homomorphism from a commutative ring to one field, then it also splits under a homomorphism from that same ring to another field.
explanatories.AlgHom.rangeRestrict: The range restriction of an algebra homomorphism adjusts its codomain to only include the image of the original mapping.

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHomEquivAlgHomOfS.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSplits (L : Type*) [Field L]     [Algebra F L] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower F L A]     (hL : ∀ x : K, (minpoly F x).Splits (algebraMap F L)) :     (K →ₐ[F] L) ≃ (K →ₐ[F] A) :=   (AlgEquiv.refl.arrowCongr (AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L A))).trans <|     IntermediateField.algHomEquivAlgHomOfSplits A (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L A).fieldRange     fun x ↦ splits_of_algHom (hL x) (AlgHom.rangeRestrict _)
Algebra.IsAlgebraic.algHomEquivAlgHomOfS.description: This definition establishes a correspondence between the embeddings of one field into another and a subextension where the minimal polynomials of the original field's elements can be split.

spectrum.subset_polynomial_aeval.code:
spectrum.subset_polynomial_aeval.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] (a : A) (p : 𝕜[X]) :
  (fun x => eval x p) '' σ a ⊆ σ ((aeval a) p)
spectrum.subset_polynomial_aeval.comment:
Half of the spectral mapping theorem for polynomials. We prove it separately
because it holds over any field, whereas `spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_pos` and
`spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempty` need the field to be algebraically closed.

explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.eval: This definition establishes a function that computes the value of a polynomial at a given point in a semiring.

spectrum.subset_polynomial_aeval.description: The set of evaluations of a polynomial at points in the spectrum of an algebra over a field is a subset of the spectrum of the polynomial evaluated at a specific element of the algebra.

spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_.code:
spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_pos.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A]
  [IsAlgClosed 𝕜] (a : A) (p : 𝕜[X]) (hdeg : 0 < p.degree) : σ ((aeval a) p) = (fun x => eval x p) '' σ a
spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_.comment:
The *spectral mapping theorem* for polynomials.  Note: the assumption `degree p > 0`
is necessary in case `σ a = ∅`, for then the left-hand side is `∅` and the right-hand side,
assuming `[Nontrivial A]`, is `{k}` where `p = Polynomial.C k`.

explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.eval: This definition establishes a function that computes the value of a polynomial at a given point in a semiring.

spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_degree_.description: The spectral mapping theorem states that for a polynomial with positive degree, the image of its evaluation at a given point corresponds to the set of images of the roots of the polynomial evaluated at that point.

spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempt.code:
spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempty.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A]
  [IsAlgClosed 𝕜] (a : A) (p : 𝕜[X]) (hnon : (σ a).Nonempty) : σ ((aeval a) p) = (fun k => eval k p) '' σ a
spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempt.comment:
In this version of the spectral mapping theorem, we assume the spectrum
is nonempty instead of assuming the degree of the polynomial is positive.

explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.eval: This definition establishes a function that computes the value of a polynomial at a given point in a semiring.

spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempt.description: For a nonempty spectrum of an element, the image of its evaluation under a polynomial corresponds to the spectrum of the polynomial evaluated at that element.

spectrum.pow_image_subset.code:
spectrum.pow_image_subset.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] (a : A) (n : ℕ) :
  (fun x => x ^ n) '' σ a ⊆ σ (a ^ n)
spectrum.pow_image_subset.comment: A specialization of `spectrum.subset_polynomial_aeval` to monic monomials for convenience.
spectrum.pow_image_subset.description: The image of the set of all n-th powers of the roots of a number under the polynomial spectrum is contained within the spectrum of the n-th power of that number.

spectrum.map_pow_of_pos.code:
spectrum.map_pow_of_pos.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] [IsAlgClosed 𝕜] (a : A)
  {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : σ (a ^ n) = (fun x => x ^ n) '' σ a
spectrum.map_pow_of_pos.comment:
A specialization of `spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempty` to monic monomials for
convenience.
spectrum.map_pow_of_pos.description: The theorem states that for a positive integer exponent, the spectrum of a power of an element is equal to the image of the spectrum of that element under the function that raises each element to the given exponent.

spectrum.map_pow_of_nonempty.code:
spectrum.map_pow_of_nonempty.{u, v} {𝕜 : Type u} {A : Type v} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] [IsAlgClosed 𝕜] {a : A}
  (ha : (σ a).Nonempty) (n : ℕ) : σ (a ^ n) = (fun x => x ^ n) '' σ a
spectrum.map_pow_of_nonempty.comment:
A specialization of `spectrum.map_polynomial_aeval_of_nonempty` to monic monomials for
convenience.
spectrum.map_pow_of_nonempty.description: If the spectrum of an element is nonempty, the spectrum of its power is equal to the image of its spectrum under the operation of raising each element to that power.

Every element `a` in a nontrivial finite-dimensional algebra `A`

spectrum.nonempty_of_isAlgClosed_of_fini.description: Every element in a nontrivial finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field has a non-empty spectrum.

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.cardinal_mk_le_sigma.description: This theorem establishes that the cardinality of a domain is less than or equal to the cardinality of the product of its polynomial ring and the set of its roots in an algebraically closed field.

explanatories.MvPolynomial.cardinal_mk_le_max: This theorem establishes that the cardinality of the multivariate polynomial ring is bounded above by the maximum of the cardinalities of the semiring, the variable type, and infinity.

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.cardinal_mk_le_max.description: This theorem indicates that the cardinality of an algebraic extension is limited to the greater value between the cardinality of the base ring and the smallest infinite cardinal.

explanatories.IsTranscendenceBasis: A family of elements is considered a transcendence basis if it is the largest subset that remains algebraically independent over a given commutative ring.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

IsAlgClosed.isAlgClosure_of_transcendenc.description: This theorem asserts that the algebraic closure of the set of elements generated by a transcendence basis over a commutative ring is indeed an algebraic closure in the larger field.

IsAlgClosed.equivOfTranscendenceBasis.comment:
setting `R` to be `ZMod (ringChar R)` this result shows that if two algebraically
closed fields have equipotent transcendence bases and the same characteristic then they are
isomorphic.

explanatories.AlgEquiv.toRingEquiv: This definition describes a conversion from an algebraic equivalence between two algebras over a commutative semiring to a ring equivalence between those algebras.
explanatories.RingEquiv.trans: This defines a construction that allows the composition of two ring equivalences to produce a new ring equivalence between the original and the final structures.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom: This definition asserts that if there exists an algebra homomorphism between two algebras and its inverse, then the two algebras are isomorphic as algebras over the given commutative semiring.

AlgebraicClosure.toSplittingField.fullDefinition: def toSplittingField (s : Finset (MonicIrreducible k)) :     MvPolynomial (MonicIrreducible k) k →ₐ[k] SplittingField (∏ x ∈ s, x : k[X]) :=   MvPolynomial.aeval fun f =>     if hf : f ∈ s then       rootOfSplits _         ((splits_prod_iff _ fun (j : MonicIrreducible k) _ => j.2.2.ne_zero).1           (SplittingField.splits _) f hf)         (mt isUnit_iff_degree_eq_zero.2 f.2.2.not_unit)     else 37
AlgebraicClosure.toSplittingField.description: This definition constructs an algebra homomorphism from a multivariate polynomial ring to the splitting field of the product of a given set of monic irreducible polynomials, mapping each variable to a root of its corresponding polynomial.

Field.finSepDegree.code: Field.finSepDegree.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] : ℕ
Field.finSepDegree.comment:
If `E / F` is an algebraic extension, then the (finite) separable degree of `E / F`
is the number of `F`-algebra homomorphisms from `E` to the algebraic closure of `E`,
as a natural number. It is defined to be zero if there are infinitely many of them.
Note that if `E / F` is not algebraic, then this definition makes no mathematical sense.

Field.finSepDegree.description: The finite separable degree of an algebraic extension between two fields quantifies the number of algebra homomorphisms from the extension field to its algebraic closure, with a value of zero assigned when there are infinitely many such homomorphisms.

Field.embEquivOfEquiv.fullDefinition: def embEquivOfEquiv (i : E ≃ₐ[F] K) :     Emb F E ≃ Emb F K := AlgEquiv.arrowCongr i <| AlgEquiv.symm <| by   let _ : Algebra E K := i.toAlgHom.toRingHom.toAlgebra   have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic E K := by     constructor     intro x     have h := isAlgebraic_algebraMap (R := E) (A := K) (i.symm.toAlgHom x)     rw [show ∀ y : E, (algebraMap E K) y = i.toAlgHom y from fun y ↦ rfl] at h     simpa only [AlgEquiv.toAlgHom_eq_coe, AlgHom.coe_coe, AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using h   apply AlgEquiv.restrictScalars (R := F) (S := E)   exact IsAlgClosure.equivOfAlgebraic E K (AlgebraicClosure K) (AlgebraicClosure E)
Field.embEquivOfEquiv.description: This defines a bijection between the sets of algebra homomorphisms from one field extension to its algebraic closure and another isomorphic field extension, reflecting the underlying algebraic structure.

Field.embEquivOfAdjoinSplits.comment:
A random bijection between `Field.Emb F E` and `E →ₐ[F] K` if `E = F(S)` such that every
element `s` of `S` is integral (= algebraic) over `F` and whose minimal polynomial splits in `K`.
Combined with `Field.instInhabitedEmb`, it can be viewed as a stronger version of

explanatories.Field.Emb: The type represents algebra homomorphisms from a field to its algebraic closure, characterizing how elements from one field can be expressed in terms of another field.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IntermediateField.adjoin: The adjoin operation extends a field by incorporating a specified set of elements from a larger field.
explanatories.IsIntegral: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is defined as integral if it can be expressed as a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients from that ring.
explanatories.Polynomial.Splits: A polynomial is said to split if it is either zero or all of its irreducible factors have a degree of one.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.isAlgebraic: This theorem asserts that if there is an algebraic equivalence between two algebras over a ring, the algebraic nature of one algebra is preserved in the other.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.antisymm: If there are embeddings from one type to another and from the second type back to the first, then there exists an equivalence between the two types.
explanatories.IntermediateField.mem_top: Every element of the extension field is contained in the top element of the lattice of intermediate fields over that base field.
explanatories.IsAlgClosed.splits_codomain: This theorem states that a polynomial over a field extension can be split into linear factors if the base field is algebraically closed.
explanatories.LE.le.antisymm: A theorem asserting that in a partially ordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements are equal.
explanatories.IsAlgebraic: This definition describes an element in an R-algebra as being algebraic over R if it satisfies a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients from R.
explanatories.IsIntegral.isAlgebraic: This theorem asserts that if an element in an R-algebra is integral over the ring R, then it is also algebraic over R.

Field.embEquivOfAdjoinSplits.fullDefinition: def embEquivOfAdjoinSplits {S : Set E} (hS : adjoin F S = ⊤)     (hK : ∀ s ∈ S, IsIntegral F s ∧ Splits (algebraMap F K) (minpoly F s)) :     Emb F E ≃ (E →ₐ[F] K) :=   have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F (⊤ : IntermediateField F E) :=     (hS ▸ isAlgebraic_adjoin (S := S) fun x hx ↦ (hK x hx).1)   have halg := (topEquiv (F := F) (E := E)).isAlgebraic   Classical.choice <| Function.Embedding.antisymm     (halg.algHomEmbeddingOfSplits (fun _ ↦ splits_of_mem_adjoin F (S := S) hK (hS ▸ mem_top)) _)     (halg.algHomEmbeddingOfSplits (fun _ ↦ IsAlgClosed.splits_codomain _) _)
Field.embEquivOfAdjoinSplits.description: There exists a bijective correspondence between algebra homomorphisms from a field to an extension field and algebra homomorphisms from that extension field to another field, under the condition that the extension is generated by integral elements whose minimal polynomials split in the target field.

Field.embEquivOfIsAlgClosed.code:

  [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] [IsAlgClosed K] : Emb F E ≃ (E →ₐ[F] K)
Field.embEquivOfIsAlgClosed.comment:

explanatories.Field.Emb: The type represents algebra homomorphisms from a field to its algebraic closure, characterizing how elements from one field can be expressed in terms of another field.
explanatories.IsAlgClosed.splits_codomain: This theorem states that a polynomial over a field extension can be split into linear factors if the base field is algebraically closed.

explanatories.IntermediateField.adjoin_univ: The theorem states that the algebra generated by a field over the entire set of elements in an algebra is equal to the largest possible intermediate field.
explanatories.Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral: If an algebra over a commutative ring is integral, then every element of that algebra is also integral over the commutative ring.
explanatories.IsAlgebraic: This definition describes an element in an R-algebra as being algebraic over R if it satisfies a nonzero polynomial equation with coefficients from R.
