IsPurelyInseparable.pow_mem.{u, v} (F : Type u) {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] (x : E) : ∃ n, x ^ q ^ n ∈ (algebraMap F E).range

explanatories.RingHom.range: The range of a ring homomorphism is defined as a subring within the target ring.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

IsPurelyInseparable.pow_mem.description: In a purely inseparable field extension, any element can be expressed as a power of a root of an element from the base field raised to a certain exponent.

IsPurelyInseparable.injective_comp_algeb.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.injective_comp_algebraMap.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] (L : Type w) [CommRing L] [IsReduced L] :
  Function.Injective fun f => f.comp (algebraMap F E)
IsPurelyInseparable.injective_comp_algeb.comment:
If `E / F` is purely inseparable, then for any reduced ring `L`, the map `(E →+* L) → (F →+* L)`
induced by `algebraMap F E` is injective. In particular, a purely inseparable field extension
is an epimorphism in the category of fields.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.LinearIndependent.comp: If a family of vectors is linearly independent over a ring, then its composition with an injective function maintains linear independence.

IsPurelyInseparable.injective_comp_algeb.description: A purely inseparable field extension ensures that the induced map from the homomorphisms of the extension to those of the base field is injective when combining with a reduced ring.

instUniqueAlgHomOfIsPurelyInseparable.code:
instUniqueAlgHomOfIsPurelyInseparable.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] (L : Type w) [CommRing L] [IsReduced L] [Algebra F L] [Algebra E L] [IsScalarTower F E L] :
  Unique (E →ₐ[F] L)

explanatories.AlgEquiv.toAlgHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebraic equivalence between two algebras over a commutative semiring as an algebra homomorphism between them.
explanatories.uniqueOfSubsingleton: If a type has only one element due to being a subsingleton, then it can be shown to have a unique instance.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.toAlgHom: This definition states that in a scalar tower, there exists a canonical algebra homomorphism from the middle element to the top element that respects the structure of the bottom element.

instUniqueAlgHomOfIsPurelyInseparable.fullDefinition: instance instUniqueAlgHomOfIsPurelyInseparable [IsPurelyInseparable F E] (L : Type w)     [CommRing L] [IsReduced L] [Algebra F L] [Algebra E L] [IsScalarTower F E L] :     Unique (E →ₐ[F] L) := uniqueOfSubsingleton (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F E L)
instUniqueAlgHomOfIsPurelyInseparable.description: If a field extension is purely inseparable over a base field and extends to a unique algebraic homomorphism into any reduced commutative ring that is in the context of a scalar tower, then this homomorphism is unique.

IsPurelyInseparable.insepDegree_eq.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.insepDegree_eq.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : insepDegree F E = Module.rank F E
IsPurelyInseparable.insepDegree_eq.comment: A purely inseparable extension has inseparable degree equal to degree.

explanatories.Field.insepDegree: The infinite inseparable degree of a field extension is defined as the degree of the extension formed by factoring out the separable closure of the base field.
explanatories.Module.rank: This defines the rank of a module as the supremum of the cardinalities of its linearly independent subsets, aligning with the dimension of a vector space for free modules over certain types of rings.

IsPurelyInseparable.insepDegree_eq.description: In a purely inseparable field extension, the inseparable degree is equal to the dimension of the extension as a module over the base field.

IsPurelyInseparable.finSepDegree_eq_one.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.finSepDegree_eq_one.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : finSepDegree F E = 1
IsPurelyInseparable.finSepDegree_eq_one.comment: A purely inseparable extension has finite separable degree one.

explanatories.Field.finSepDegree: The finite separable degree of an algebraic extension between two fields quantifies the number of algebra homomorphisms from the extension field to its algebraic closure, with a value of zero assigned when there are infinitely many such homomorphisms.

IsPurelyInseparable.finSepDegree_eq_one.description: A purely inseparable field extension has a finite separable degree of one.

isPurelyInseparable_of_finSepDegree_eq_o.code:
isPurelyInseparable_of_finSepDegree_eq_one.{u, v} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] (hdeg : finSepDegree F E = 1) : IsPurelyInseparable F E
isPurelyInseparable_of_finSepDegree_eq_o.comment: If an algebraic extension has finite separable degree one, then it is purely inseparable.

explanatories.Field.finSepDegree: The finite separable degree of an algebraic extension between two fields quantifies the number of algebra homomorphisms from the extension field to its algebraic closure, with a value of zero assigned when there are infinitely many such homomorphisms.

isPurelyInseparable_of_finSepDegree_eq_o.description: An algebraic field extension with a finite separable degree of one is purely inseparable.

IsPurelyInseparable.tower_bot.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.tower_bot.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (K : Type w)
  [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [IsPurelyInseparable F K] : IsPurelyInseparable F E
IsPurelyInseparable.tower_bot.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower such that `K / F` is purely inseparable,
then `E / F` is also purely inseparable.
IsPurelyInseparable.tower_bot.description: In a tower of field extensions where the top extension is purely inseparable over the base, the intermediate extension is also purely inseparable.

IsPurelyInseparable.minpoly_eq_X_sub_C_p.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.minpoly_eq_X_sub_C_pow.{u, v} (F : Type u) {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (q : ℕ)
  [ExpChar F q] [IsPurelyInseparable F E] (x : E) :
  ∃ n, Polynomial.map (algebraMap F E) (minpoly F x) = (X - C x) ^ q ^ n

explanatories.IntermediateField.map: This definition describes how to construct a new intermediate field from an existing one by applying an algebra homomorphism between the two corresponding fields.
explanatories.Polynomial.C: This definition specifies a ring homomorphism that maps a constant from a semiring to the corresponding constant polynomial in a polynomial ring.
explanatories.Polynomial.map: This definition describes a process for transforming a polynomial from one semiring to another using a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.Monic.map: This theorem states that if a polynomial is monic in one semiring, then its image under a ring homomorphism to another semiring is also monic.

IsPurelyInseparable.minpoly_eq_X_sub_C_p.description: In a purely inseparable extension, the minimal polynomial of any element can be expressed as a power of a specific polynomial form involving that element and a characteristic exponent.

separableClosure_le.code:
separableClosure_le.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (L : IntermediateField F E)
  [h : IsPurelyInseparable (↥L) E] : separableClosure F E ≤ L
separableClosure_le.comment:
An intermediate field of `E / F` contains the separable closure of `F` in `E`
if `E` is purely inseparable over it.
separableClosure_le.description: If an intermediate field is purely inseparable over a base field extension, then it contains the separable closure of the base field.

separableClosure.isPurelyInseparable.code:
separableClosure.isPurelyInseparable.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] : IsPurelyInseparable (↥(separableClosure F E)) E
separableClosure.isPurelyInseparable.comment:
If `E / F` is algebraic, then `E` is purely inseparable over the
separable closure of `F` in `E`.

explanatories.AlgEquiv.isPurelyInseparable: If a field extension is purely inseparable over one algebra that is isomorphic to another algebra via an algebra isomorphism, then the second algebra is also purely inseparable over the same base field.

separableClosure.isPurelyInseparable.description: If a field extension is algebraic, then its elements are purely inseparable over the separable closure of the base field within that extension.

IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (K : Type w)
  [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [h : IsPurelyInseparable F K] : IsPurelyInseparable E K
IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower such that `K / F` is purely inseparable,
then `K / E` is also purely inseparable.

explanatories.Algebra.IsAlgebraic.tower_top: This theorem demonstrates that if an algebra is algebraic over a field, it remains algebraic when considered over an extension of that field.
explanatories.IsAlgebraic.tower_top: This theorem states that if an element is algebraic over a field, then it remains algebraic when considered over an extension of that field.
explanatories.IsIntegral.tower_top: If an element is integral over a commutative ring in an algebra tower, then it is also integral over the intermediate algebra.

IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top.description: If a field extension tower is such that the top extension is purely inseparable over the base field, then the intermediate extension is also purely inseparable.

eq_separableClosure.code:
eq_separableClosure.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] (L : IntermediateField F E)
  [Algebra.IsSeparable F ↥L] [IsPurelyInseparable (↥L) E] : L = separableClosure F E
eq_separableClosure.comment:
If an intermediate field of `E / F` is separable over `F`, and `E` is purely inseparable
over it, then it is equal to the separable closure of `F` in `E`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

eq_separableClosure.description: If an intermediate field is separable over a base field and the larger field extension is purely inseparable over that intermediate field, then the intermediate field coincides with the separable closure of the base field within the extension.

mem_perfectClosure_iff_natSepDegree_eq_o.code:
mem_perfectClosure_iff_natSepDegree_eq_one.{u, v} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] {x : E} :
  x ∈ perfectClosure F E ↔ (minpoly F x).natSepDegree = 1
mem_perfectClosure_iff_natSepDegree_eq_o.comment:
An element is contained in the relative perfect closure if and only if its mininal polynomial
has separable degree one.

explanatories.Polynomial.natSepDegree: The separable degree of a polynomial is defined as the number of distinct roots it has in its splitting field, which is always a non-negative integer.

mem_perfectClosure_iff_natSepDegree_eq_o.description: An element belongs to the relative perfect closure of a field extension if and only if its minimal polynomial has a separable degree equal to one.

IntermediateField.isPurelyInseparable_ad.code:
IntermediateField.isPurelyInseparable_adjoin_iff_pow_mem.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (q : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {S : Set E} :
  IsPurelyInseparable F ↥(adjoin F S) ↔ ∀ x ∈ S, ∃ n, x ^ q ^ n ∈ (algebraMap F E).range
IntermediateField.isPurelyInseparable_ad.comment:
If `F` is of exponential characteristic `q`, then `F(S) / F` is a purely inseparable extension
if and only if for any `x ∈ S`, `x ^ (q ^ n)` is contained in `F` for some `n : ℕ`.

explanatories.RingHom.range: The range of a ring homomorphism is defined as a subring within the target ring.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

IntermediateField.isPurelyInseparable_ad.description: A field extension generated by a set is purely inseparable if and only if each element in that set raised to a power depending on the characteristic is contained in the image of the algebra map from the base field.

IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.code:
IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (S : Set E) [Algebra.IsSeparable F ↥(adjoin F S)] (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (n : ℕ) :
  adjoin F S = adjoin F ((fun x => x ^ q ^ n) '' S)
IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.comment:
If `F` is a field of exponential characteristic `q`, `F(S) / F` is separable, then
`F(S) = F(S ^ (q ^ n))` for any natural number `n`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.description: In a field with exponential characteristic, if an extension generated by a set is separable, then it can be represented as the adjoin of the set raised to a particular power.

IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.code:
IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable'.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (S : Set E) (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (n : ℕ) :
  adjoin F S = adjoin F ((fun x => x ^ q ^ n) '' S)
IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.comment:
If `E / F` is a separable field extension of exponential characteristic `q`, then
`F(S) = F(S ^ (q ^ n))` for any subset `S` of `E` and any natural number `n`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

IntermediateField.adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_e.description: In a separable field extension with exponential characteristic, any extension generated by a set can be expressed as the extension generated by that set raised to a specific power.

Field.span_map_pow_expChar_pow_eq_top_of.code:
Field.span_map_pow_expChar_pow_eq_top_of_isSeparable.{u, v, u_1} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (q n : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {ι : Type u_1} {v : ι → E} [Algebra.IsSeparable F E]
  (h : Submodule.span F (Set.range v) = ⊤) : Submodule.span F (Set.range fun x => v x ^ q ^ n) = ⊤
Field.span_map_pow_expChar_pow_eq_top_of.comment:
If `E / F` is a separable extension of exponential characteristic `q`, if `{ u_i }` is a family
of elements of `E` which `F`-linearly spans `E`, then `{ u_i ^ (q ^ n) }` also `F`-linearly spans
`E` for any natural number `n`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.RingHom.range: The range of a ring homomorphism is defined as a subring within the target ring.
explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Field.span_map_pow_expChar_pow_eq_top_of.description: In a separable field extension of exponential characteristic, if a family of elements spans the entire extension, then the same family raised to a specific power will also span the extension.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code:
LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of_fd_isSeparable.{u, v, u_1} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (q n : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {ι : Type u_1} {v : ι → E} [FiniteDimensional F E]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (h : LinearIndependent F v) : LinearIndependent F fun x => v x ^ q ^ n
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment:
If `E / F` is a finite separable extension of exponential characteristic `q`, if `{ u_i }` is a
family of elements of `E` which is `F`-linearly independent, then `{ u_i ^ (q ^ n) }` is also
`F`-linearly independent for any natural number `n`. A special case of
`LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable`
and is an intermediate result used to prove it.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: If a finite separable extension maintains linear independence of a set of elements, then raising those elements to the power of the characteristic of the base field raised to any natural number preserves that linear independence.

LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.code:
LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable.{u, v, u_1} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (q n : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {ι : Type u_1} {v : ι → E} [Algebra.IsSeparable F E]
  (h : LinearIndependent F v) : LinearIndependent F fun x => v x ^ q ^ n
LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.comment:
If `E / F` is a separable extension of exponential characteristic `q`, if `{ u_i }` is a
family of elements of `E` which is `F`-linearly independent, then `{ u_i ^ (q ^ n) }` is also
`F`-linearly independent for any natural number `n`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.description: In a separable field extension with exponential characteristic, if a set of elements is linearly independent, then raising each element to a power of the characteristic maintains their linear independence.

Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_.code:
Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_of_isSepClosed.{u, v} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] [IsSepClosed F] : IsPurelyInseparable F E
Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_.comment:
If `E / F` is an algebraic extension, `F` is separably closed,
then `E / F` is purely inseparable.
Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isPurelyInseparable_.description: If a field extension is algebraic and the base field is separably closed, then the extension is purely inseparable.

separableClosure.eq_bot_iff.code:
separableClosure.eq_bot_iff.{u, v} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] : separableClosure F E = ⊥ ↔ IsPurelyInseparable F E
separableClosure.eq_bot_iff.comment:
If `E / F` is an algebraic extension, then the separable closure of `F` in `E` is
equal to `F` if and only if `E / F` is purely inseparable.
separableClosure.eq_bot_iff.description: The separable closure of a field extension equals the base field if and only if the extension is purely inseparable.

isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_alge.code:
isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_algebraicClosure.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsAlgClosure F E] : IsSepClosed F ↔ IsPurelyInseparable F E
isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_alge.comment:
If `E` is an algebraic closure of `F`, then `F` is separably closed if and only if `E / F` is
purely inseparable.
isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_alge.description: A field is separably closed if and only if its algebraic closure is purely inseparable.

perfectField_of_perfectClosure_eq_bot.code:
perfectField_of_perfectClosure_eq_bot.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [h : PerfectField E] (eq : perfectClosure F E = ⊥) : PerfectField F

explanatories.ringExpChar.eq: The exponential characteristic of a semiring is equal to a given natural number if that semiring possesses that exponential characteristic.

perfectField_of_perfectClosure_eq_bot.description: If a field is perfect and its perfect closure is trivial, then the base field is also perfect.

perfectClosure.eq_bot_of_isSeparable.code:
perfectClosure.eq_bot_of_isSeparable.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : perfectClosure F E = ⊥
perfectClosure.eq_bot_of_isSeparable.comment:
If `E / F` is separable, then the perfect closure of `F` in `E` is equal to `F`. Note that
the converse is not necessarily true (see https://math.stackexchange.com/a/3009197)
even when `E / F` is algebraic.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

perfectClosure.eq_bot_of_isSeparable.description: If a field extension is separable, then its perfect closure within the extension is equal to the original field.

perfectField_of_isSeparable_of_perfectFi.code:
perfectField_of_isSeparable_of_perfectField_top.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] [PerfectField E] : PerfectField F
perfectField_of_isSeparable_of_perfectFi.comment: If `E / F` is a separable extension, `E` is perfect, then `F` is also prefect.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

perfectField_of_isSeparable_of_perfectFi.description: A field is perfect if it has a separable extension to another perfect field.

Field.finSepDegree_eq.code:
Field.finSepDegree_eq.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] :
  finSepDegree F E = Cardinal.toNat (sepDegree F E)
Field.finSepDegree_eq.comment:
If `E / F` is algebraic, then the `Field.finSepDegree F E` is equal to `Field.sepDegree F E`
as a natural number. This means that the cardinality of `Field.Emb F E` and the degree of
`(separableClosure F E) / F` are both finite or infinite, and when they are finite, they
coincide.

explanatories.Cardinal.toNat: This defines a function that converts finite cardinals to their natural number equivalents while mapping infinite cardinals to zero.

Field.finSepDegree_eq.description: If a field extension is algebraic, then the finite separation degree of the extension is equal to the separation degree expressed as a natural number.

Field.finInsepDegree.eq_1.code:
Field.finInsepDegree.eq_1.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] :
  finInsepDegree F E = finrank (↥(separableClosure F E)) E

explanatories.IsSeparable.eq_1: An element in an algebraic structure is separable over a field if and only if its minimal polynomial is separable.
explanatories.IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank: The finite rank of the field obtained by adjoining an integral element to a base field equals the degree of its minimal polynomial over that base field.
explanatories.Field.sepDegree.eq_1: The infinite separable degree of a field extension is equal to the rank of the module formed by the separable closure of the extended field over the base field.
explanatories.Field.insepDegree.eq_1: The inseparable degree of a field extension is equal to the rank of the extension when viewed over its separable closure.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.Finsupp.sum.eq_1: The sum of a function evaluated at a finitely supported function is equal to the sum of that function evaluated at each element in the support of the finitely supported function, weighted by its values.

Field.finInsepDegree.eq_1.description: The finite inseparable degree of a field extension equals the finite rank of its separable closure over the extension.

separableClosure.adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebrai.code:
separableClosure.adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebraic_of_isSeparable.{u, v, w} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable E K] : adjoin E ↑(separableClosure F K) = ⊤
separableClosure.adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebrai.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is algebraic and `K / E`
is separable, then `E` adjoin `separableClosure F K` is equal to `K`. It is a special case of
`separableClosure.adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebraic`, and is an intermediate result used to prove it.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.IntermediateField.adjoin: The adjoin operation extends a field by incorporating a specified set of elements from a larger field.

separableClosure.adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebrai.description: In a field extension tower where one field is algebraic over another and the subsequent extension is separable, adjoining the separable closure of the first field to the intermediate field results in the entire field.

LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.code:
LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of_isIntegral'.{u, v, u_1} {F : Type u} {E : Type v} [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (q n : ℕ) [hF : ExpChar F q] {ι : Type u_1} {v : ι → E} (hsep : ∀ (i : ι), IsSeparable F (v i))
  (h : LinearIndependent F v) : LinearIndependent F fun x => v x ^ q ^ n
LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.comment:
If `E / F` is a field extension of exponential characteristic `q`, if `{ u_i }` is a
family of separable elements of `E` which is `F`-linearly independent, then `{ u_i ^ (q ^ n) }`
is also `F`-linearly independent for any natural number `n`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

LinearIndependent.map_pow_expChar_pow_of.description: If a field extension has exponential characteristic and a set of separable elements is linearly independent, then the set formed by raising those elements to a power that is a power of the characteristic remains linearly independent.

LinearIndependent.map_of_isPurelyInsepar.code:
LinearIndependent.map_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isSeparable.{u, v, w, u_1} {F : Type u} (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] {K : Type w} [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [IsPurelyInseparable F E]
  {ι : Type u_1} {v : ι → K} (hsep : ∀ (i : ι), IsSeparable F (v i)) (h : LinearIndependent F v) : LinearIndependent E v

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.

LinearIndependent.map_of_isPurelyInsepar.description: In a field extension tower where one extension is purely inseparable, a family of separable elements that is linearly independent over the base field remains linearly independent over the intermediate field.

Field.lift_rank_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_is.code:
Field.lift_rank_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_isSeparable.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] :
  Cardinal.lift.{w, v} (Module.rank F E) * Cardinal.lift.{v, w} (sepDegree E K) = Cardinal.lift.{v, w} (sepDegree F K)
Field.lift_rank_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_is.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is separable,
then $[E:F] [K:E]_s = [K:F]_s$.
It is a special case of `Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_isAlgebraic`, and is an
intermediate result used to prove it.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.Module.rank: This defines the rank of a module as the supremum of the cardinalities of its linearly independent subsets, aligning with the dimension of a vector space for free modules over certain types of rings.

Field.lift_rank_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_is.description: The product of the rank of a separable field extension and the separable degree of a larger extension equals the separable degree from the base field to the largest field in the extension tower.

Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.code:
Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isSeparable.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [IsPurelyInseparable F E]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable E K] : sepDegree F K = Module.rank E K
Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is purely inseparable and `K / E`
is separable, then the separable degree of `K / F` is equal to the degree of `K / E`.
It is a special case of `Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_isAlgebraic`, and is an
intermediate result used to prove it.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.Module.rank: This defines the rank of a module as the supremum of the cardinalities of its linearly independent subsets, aligning with the dimension of a vector space for free modules over certain types of rings.

Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.description: The separable degree of a field extension from the base field to an intermediate field is equal to the module rank of the intermediate field over the field extension when the intermediate field is purely inseparable over the base field and the extension is separable.

Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.code:
Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparable.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [IsPurelyInseparable F E] :
  sepDegree F K = sepDegree E K
Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is purely inseparable,
then $[K:F]_s = [K:E]_s$.
It is a special case of `Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_isAlgebraic`, and is an
intermediate result used to prove it.
Field.sepDegree_eq_of_isPurelyInseparabl.description: The separable degree of an extension from a purely inseparable field is the same whether calculated from the base field or the intermediate field.

Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_.code:
Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_of_isAlgebraic.{u, v, w} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] :
  Cardinal.lift.{w, v} (sepDegree F E) * Cardinal.lift.{v, w} (sepDegree E K) = Cardinal.lift.{v, w} (sepDegree F K)
Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is algebraic, then their
separable degrees satisfy the tower law: $[E:F]_s [K:E]_s = [K:F]_s$.
Field.lift_sepDegree_mul_lift_sepDegree_.description: In an algebraic field extension tower, the separable degrees of the extensions satisfy the multiplicative property defined by the tower law.

IsPurelyInseparable.sepDegree_eq_one.code:
IsPurelyInseparable.sepDegree_eq_one.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : sepDegree F E = 1
IsPurelyInseparable.sepDegree_eq_one.comment: A purely inseparable extension has separable degree one.

explanatories.Field.sepDegree: The infinite separable degree of a field extension is defined as the degree of the extension formed by taking the separable closure of the extended field over the base field.

IsPurelyInseparable.sepDegree_eq_one.description: A purely inseparable field extension has a separable degree equal to one.

Field.sepDegree_mul_sepDegree_of_isAlgeb.code:
Field.sepDegree_mul_sepDegree_of_isAlgebraic.{u, v} (F : Type u) (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] :
  sepDegree F E * sepDegree E K = sepDegree F K
Field.sepDegree_mul_sepDegree_of_isAlgeb.description: In an algebraic field extension tower, the separation degree of the base field over the first extension multiplied by the separation degree of the first extension over the second equals the separation degree of the base field over the second extension.

IntermediateField.sepDegree_adjoin_eq_of.code:
IntermediateField.sepDegree_adjoin_eq_of_isAlgebraic_of_isPurelyInseparable.{u, v, w} {F : Type u} (E : Type v)
  [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] {K : Type w} [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (S : Set K)
  [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F ↥(adjoin F S)] [IsPurelyInseparable F E] :
  sepDegree E ↥(adjoin E S) = sepDegree F ↥(adjoin F S)
IntermediateField.sepDegree_adjoin_eq_of.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is purely inseparable, then
for any subset `S` of `K` such that `F(S) / F` is algebraic, the `E(S) / E` and `F(S) / F` have
the same separable degree.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

IntermediateField.sepDegree_adjoin_eq_of.description: In a field extension tower where the extension from one field to another is purely inseparable, the separable degrees of adjoining a set of elements from those fields remain equal when the base field's adjoining set is algebraic.

minpoly.map_eq_of_isSeparable_of_isPurel.code:
minpoly.map_eq_of_isSeparable_of_isPurelyInseparable.{u, v, w} {F : Type u} (E : Type v) [Field F] [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] {K : Type w} [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (x : K)
  (hsep : IsSeparable F x) [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : Polynomial.map (algebraMap F E) (minpoly F x) = minpoly E x
minpoly.map_eq_of_isSeparable_of_isPurel.comment:
If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is purely inseparable, then
for any element `x` of `K` separable over `F`, it has the same minimal polynomials over `F` and
over `E`.

explanatories.IsSeparable: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is considered separable if its minimal polynomial over the algebra is separable.
explanatories.IntermediateField.map: This definition describes how to construct a new intermediate field from an existing one by applying an algebra homomorphism between the two corresponding fields.
explanatories.Polynomial.map: This definition describes a process for transforming a polynomial from one semiring to another using a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.Monic.map: This theorem states that if a polynomial is monic in one semiring, then its image under a ring homomorphism to another semiring is also monic.

minpoly.map_eq_of_isSeparable_of_isPurel.description: If a field extension is purely inseparable and an element is separable over the base field, then the minimal polynomial of that element remains unchanged when considered over either field in the extension tower.

pNilradical.code: pNilradical.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R] (p : ℕ) : Ideal R
pNilradical.comment:
Given a natural number `p`, the `p`-nilradical of a ring is defined to be the
nilradical if `p > 1` (`pNilradical_eq_nilradical`), and defined to be the zero ideal if `p ≤ 1`
(`pNilradical_eq_bot'`). Equivalently, it is the ideal consisting of elements `x` such that
`x ^ p ^ n = 0` for some `n` (`mem_pNilradical`).

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.nilradical: The nilradical of a commutative semiring is the ideal consisting of all nilpotent elements.

pNilradical.fullDefinition: def pNilradical (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (p : ℕ) : Ideal R := if 1 < p then nilradical R else ⊥
pNilradical.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is defined as the nilradical for values of p greater than one, and as the zero ideal for values of p less than or equal to one, consisting of elements that become zero when raised to a power that is a multiple of p.

pNilradical.eq_1.code: pNilradical.eq_1.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R] (p : ℕ) : pNilradical R p = if 1 < p then nilradical R else ⊥

explanatories.nilradical: The nilradical of a commutative semiring is the ideal consisting of all nilpotent elements.

pNilradical.eq_1.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is equal to the nilradical when p is greater than one, and to the zero ideal when p is less than or equal to one.

pNilradical_eq_bot.code: pNilradical_eq_bot.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} (hp : ¬1 < p) : pNilradical R p = ⊥
pNilradical_eq_bot.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is the zero ideal when p is not greater than one.

pNilradical_eq_nilradical.code: pNilradical_eq_nilradical.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} (hp : 1 < p) : pNilradical R p = nilradical R
pNilradical_eq_nilradical.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is equal to the nilradical when p is greater than one.

pNilradical_eq_bot'.code: pNilradical_eq_bot'.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ 1) : pNilradical R p = ⊥
pNilradical_eq_bot'.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is equal to the zero ideal when p is less than or equal to one.

mem_pNilradical.code: mem_pNilradical.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} {x : R} : x ∈ pNilradical R p ↔ ∃ n, x ^ p ^ n = 0
mem_pNilradical.description: An element belongs to the p-nilradical of a commutative semiring if and only if it can be raised to a power, multiplied by p, to yield zero.

sub_mem_pNilradical_iff_pow_expChar_pow_.code:
sub_mem_pNilradical_iff_pow_expChar_pow_eq.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {p : ℕ} [ExpChar R p] {x y : R} :
  x - y ∈ pNilradical R p ↔ ∃ n, x ^ p ^ n = y ^ p ^ n
sub_mem_pNilradical_iff_pow_expChar_pow_.description: The difference between two elements in a commutative ring belongs to the p-nilradical if and only if there exists a natural number such that raising both elements to the power of p raised to that number results in equality.

pNilradical_eq_bot_of_frobenius_inj.code:
pNilradical_eq_bot_of_frobenius_inj.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar R p]
  (h : Function.Injective ⇑(frobenius R p)) : pNilradical R p = ⊥

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

pNilradical_eq_bot_of_frobenius_inj.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative ring is the zero ideal when the Frobenius homomorphism associated with the ring is injective.

IsPRadical.pow_mem'.code:
IsPRadical.pow_mem'.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] {i : K →+* L} {p : ℕ}
  [self : IsPRadical i p] (x : L) : ∃ n y, i y = x ^ p ^ n
IsPRadical.pow_mem'.description: If a homomorphism preserves a p-radical structure, then for any element in the codomain, there exist integers and an element in the domain such that applying the homomorphism produces a power of the original element.

IsPRadical.ker_le'.code:
IsPRadical.ker_le'.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] {i : K →+* L} {p : ℕ}
  [self : IsPRadical i p] : RingHom.ker i ≤ pNilradical K p

explanatories.pNilradical: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is defined as the nilradical for values of p greater than one, and as the zero ideal for values of p less than or equal to one, consisting of elements that become zero when raised to a power that is a multiple of p.
explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.

IsPRadical.ker_le'.description: The kernel of a homomorphism that preserves a p-radical structure is contained within the p-nilradical of the domain.

IsPRadical.ker_le.code:
IsPRadical.ker_le.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ)
  [IsPRadical i p] : RingHom.ker i ≤ pNilradical K p

explanatories.pNilradical: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is defined as the nilradical for values of p greater than one, and as the zero ideal for values of p less than or equal to one, consisting of elements that become zero when raised to a power that is a multiple of p.
explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.

IsPRadical.ker_le.description: The kernel of a homomorphism that preserves a p-radical structure is contained within the p-nilradical of the domain semiring.

IsPRadical.pow_mem.code:
IsPRadical.pow_mem.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ)
  [IsPRadical i p] (x : L) : ∃ n y, i y = x ^ p ^ n
IsPRadical.pow_mem.description: An element in the codomain of a p-radical-preserving homomorphism can be expressed as a power of an element in the domain raised to a sufficiently large multiple of p.

IsPRadical.comap_pNilradical.code:
IsPRadical.comap_pNilradical.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L)
  (p : ℕ) [IsPRadical i p] : Ideal.comap i (pNilradical L p) = pNilradical K p

explanatories.Ideal.comap: The preimage of an ideal under a ring homomorphism is defined as the ideal consisting of all elements in the original ring that map into the ideal.

IsPRadical.comap_pNilradical.description: The image of the p-nilradical under a homomorphism from one commutative semiring to another is equal to the p-nilradical of the first semiring when the homomorphism preserves the p-radical property.

IsPerfectClosure.code:
IsPerfectClosure.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ)
  [ExpChar L p] [PerfectRing L p] : Prop
IsPerfectClosure.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` is a `p`-radical ring homomorphism, then it makes `L` a perfect closure
of `K`, if `L` is perfect.
In this case the kernel of `i` is equal to the `p`-nilradical of `K`
(see `IsPerfectClosure.ker_eq`).

Our definition makes it synonymous to `IsPRadical` if `PerfectRing L p` is present. A caveat is
that you need to write `[PerfectRing L p] [IsPerfectClosure i p]`. This is similar to
`PerfectRing` which has `ExpChar` as a prerequisite.
IsPerfectClosure.fullDefinition: abbrev IsPerfectClosure [PerfectRing L p] := IsPRadical i p
IsPerfectClosure.description: A p-radical ring homomorphism from one commutative semiring to another is defined as making the target semiring a perfect closure of the source semiring when the target is perfect.

RingHom.pNilradical_le_ker_of_perfectRin.code:
RingHom.pNilradical_le_ker_of_perfectRing.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L]
  (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar L p] [PerfectRing L p] : pNilradical K p ≤ RingHom.ker i
RingHom.pNilradical_le_ker_of_perfectRin.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` is a ring homomorphism of exponential characteristic `p` rings, such that `L`
is perfect, then the `p`-nilradical of `K` is contained in the kernel of `i`.

explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.

RingHom.pNilradical_le_ker_of_perfectRin.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is contained within the kernel of a homomorphism when the codomain is a perfect ring of exponential characteristic p.

PerfectRing.lift_aux.code:
PerfectRing.lift_aux.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ)
  [IsPRadical i p] (x : L) : ∃ y, i y.2 = x ^ p ^ y.1
PerfectRing.lift_aux.description: For every element in a commutative semiring homomorphism that preserves a p-radical structure, there exists a corresponding element in the domain such that the image under the homomorphism relates the elements through a power relationship involving p.

PerfectRing.liftAux.code:
PerfectRing.liftAux.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L]
  [CommSemiring M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] (x : L) : M
PerfectRing.liftAux.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` and `j : K →+* M` are ring homomorphisms of characteristic `p` rings, such that
`i` is `p`-radical (in fact only the `IsPRadical.pow_mem` is required) and `M` is a perfect ring,
then one can define a map `L → M` which maps an element `x` of `L` to `y ^ (p ^ -n)` if
`x ^ (p ^ n)` is equal to some element `y` of `K`.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.PerfectRing.lift_aux: For every element in a commutative semiring homomorphism that preserves a p-radical structure, there exists a corresponding element in the domain such that the image under the homomorphism relates the elements through a power relationship involving p.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

PerfectRing.liftAux.fullDefinition: def liftAux (x : L) : M := (iterateFrobeniusEquiv M p (Classical.choose (lift_aux i p x)).1).symm   (j (Classical.choose (lift_aux i p x)).2)
PerfectRing.liftAux.description: A map can be constructed from elements in one commutative semiring to another, under the conditions that the source and target semirings are of characteristic p, the source homomorphism is p-radical, and the target semiring is a perfect ring, allowing for transition of elements based upon power roots.

PerfectRing.liftAux.eq_1.code:
PerfectRing.liftAux.eq_1.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L]
  [CommSemiring M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] (x : L) :
  liftAux i j p x = (iterateFrobeniusEquiv M p (Classical.choose ⋯).1).symm (j (Classical.choose ⋯).2)

explanatories.pNilradical.eq_1: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is equal to the nilradical when p is greater than one, and to the zero ideal when p is less than or equal to one.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

PerfectRing.liftAux.eq_1.description: The auxiliary lifting process for two homomorphisms from a perfect ring preserves a specific structure related to the p-radical, allowing the transformation of elements through the iteration of the Frobenius endomorphism.

PerfectRing.liftAux_self_apply.code:
PerfectRing.liftAux_self_apply.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring L] (i : K →+* L)
  (p : ℕ) [ExpChar L p] [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing L p] (x : L) : liftAux i i p x = x
PerfectRing.liftAux_self_apply.description: The auxiliary lifting process for a homomorphism from a perfect ring is idempotent, meaning that applying it to an element yields the element itself.

PerfectRing.liftAux_id_apply.code:
PerfectRing.liftAux_id_apply.{u_1, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_3} [CommSemiring K] [CommSemiring M] (j : K →+* M)
  (p : ℕ) [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] (x : K) : liftAux (RingHom.id K) j p x = j x

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.

PerfectRing.liftAux_id_apply.description: The auxiliary lifting operation applied to the identity homomorphism of a commutative semiring will yield the same result as directly applying the homomorphism to an element when the codomain is a perfect ring of exponential characteristic p.

pow_expChar_pow_inj_of_pNilradical_eq_bo.code:
pow_expChar_pow_inj_of_pNilradical_eq_bot.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar R p]
  (h : pNilradical R p = ⊥) (n : ℕ) : Function.Injective fun x => x ^ p ^ n

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

pow_expChar_pow_inj_of_pNilradical_eq_bo.description: If the p-nilradical of a commutative ring is trivial, then the map sending each element to its power raised to a fixed multiple of p is injective.

IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` is `p`-radical, then for any ring `M` of exponential charactistic `p` whose
`p`-nilradical is zero, the map `(L →+* M) → (K →+* M)` induced by `i` is injective.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.

IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical.description: A p-radical ring homomorphism from one ring to another induces an injective map between the rings when the target ring has a zero p-nilradical.

pNilradical_le_nilradical.code: pNilradical_le_nilradical.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} : pNilradical R p ≤ nilradical R
pNilradical_le_nilradical.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative semiring is a subset of the nilradical, which consists of all nilpotent elements.

PerfectRing.pNilradical_eq_bot.code:
PerfectRing.pNilradical_eq_bot.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar R p] [PerfectRing R p] :
  pNilradical R p = ⊥
PerfectRing.pNilradical_eq_bot.description: The p-nilradical of a commutative ring is the zero ideal when the ring is perfect and has exponential characteristic p.

PerfectRing.liftAux_apply.code:
PerfectRing.liftAux_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p]
  (x : L) (n : ℕ) (y : K) (h : i y = x ^ p ^ n) : liftAux i j p x = (iterateFrobeniusEquiv M p n).symm (j y)
PerfectRing.liftAux_apply.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` and `j : K →+* M` are ring homomorphisms of characteristic `p` rings, such that
`i` is `p`-radical, and `M` is a perfect ring, then `PerfectRing.liftAux` is well-defined.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

PerfectRing.liftAux_apply.description: The application of a lifting function in the context of characteristic p rings preserves the structure of a p-radical homomorphism when mapped into a perfect ring.

PerfectRing.lift.code:
PerfectRing.lift.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L] [CommRing M]
  (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] :
  L →+* M
PerfectRing.lift.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` and `j : K →+* M` are ring homomorphisms of characteristic `p` rings, such that
`i` is `p`-radical, and `M` is a perfect ring, then `PerfectRing.liftAux`
is a ring homomorphism. This is similar to `IsAlgClosed.lift` and `IsSepClosed.lift`.

explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.pow_zero: This theorem asserts that any element raised to the power of zero in a monoid equals the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.pow_one: This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one yields the element itself.
explanatories.one_pow: This theorem asserts that raising the multiplicative identity to any natural number results in the multiplicative identity itself.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.map_pow: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.pow_mul: This theorem states that for any element in a monoid, raising it to the product of two natural numbers is equivalent to first raising it to one of those numbers and then raising the result to the other number.
explanatories.IsPRadical.pow_mem: An element in the codomain of a p-radical-preserving homomorphism can be expressed as a power of an element in the domain raised to a sufficiently large multiple of p.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply: This theorem verifies that applying a ring isomorphism and then its inverse yields the original element from the first ring.
explanatories.PerfectRing.liftAux: A map can be constructed from elements in one commutative semiring to another, under the conditions that the source and target semirings are of characteristic p, the source homomorphism is p-radical, and the target semiring is a perfect ring, allowing for transition of elements based upon power roots.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.iterateFrobeniusEquiv_def: The iteration of the Frobenius endomorphism applied to an element in a perfect ring corresponds to raising that element to the power of the characteristic raised to the iteration count.
explanatories.PerfectRing.liftAux_apply: The application of a lifting function in the context of characteristic p rings preserves the structure of a p-radical homomorphism when mapped into a perfect ring.
explanatories.map_one: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.map_mul: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.mul_pow: In a commutative monoid, the power of a product of two elements equals the product of their individual powers.
explanatories.iterateFrobeniusEquiv_symm_add_apply: The inverse of the iterated Frobenius automorphism for a perfect ring applied to the sum of two natural numbers is equivalent to applying the inverse separately for each number and then combining the results.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.add_pow_expChar_pow: The sum of two elements raised to a power determined by the exponential characteristic can be expressed as the sum of each element raised to that same power.

PerfectRing.lift.fullDefinition: def lift : L →+* M where   toFun := liftAux i j p   map_one' := by simp [liftAux_apply i j p 1 0 1 (by rw [one_pow, map_one])]   map_mul' x1 x2 := by     obtain ⟨n1, y1, h1⟩ := IsPRadical.pow_mem i p x1     obtain ⟨n2, y2, h2⟩ := IsPRadical.pow_mem i p x2     simp only; rw [liftAux_apply i j p _ _ _ h1, liftAux_apply i j p _ _ _ h2,       liftAux_apply i j p (x1 * x2) (n1 + n2) (y1 ^ p ^ n2 * y2 ^ p ^ n1) (by rw [map_mul,         map_pow, map_pow, h1, h2, ← pow_mul, ← pow_add, ← pow_mul, ← pow_add,         add_comm n2, mul_pow]),       map_mul, map_pow, map_pow, map_mul, ← iterateFrobeniusEquiv_def]     nth_rw 1 [iterateFrobeniusEquiv_symm_add_apply]     rw [RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply, add_comm n1, iterateFrobeniusEquiv_symm_add_apply,       ← iterateFrobeniusEquiv_def, RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply]   map_zero' := by simp [liftAux_apply i j p 0 0 0 (by rw [pow_zero, pow_one, map_zero])]   map_add' x1 x2 := by     obtain ⟨n1, y1, h1⟩ := IsPRadical.pow_mem i p x1     obtain ⟨n2, y2, h2⟩ := IsPRadical.pow_mem i p x2     simp only; rw [liftAux_apply i j p _ _ _ h1, liftAux_apply i j p _ _ _ h2,       liftAux_apply i j p (x1 + x2) (n1 + n2) (y1 ^ p ^ n2 + y2 ^ p ^ n1) (by rw [map_add,         map_pow, map_pow, h1, h2, ← pow_mul, ← pow_add, ← pow_mul, ← pow_add,         add_comm n2, add_pow_expChar_pow]),       map_add, map_pow, map_pow, map_add, ← iterateFrobeniusEquiv_def]     nth_rw 1 [iterateFrobeniusEquiv_symm_add_apply]     rw [RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply, add_comm n1, iterateFrobeniusEquiv_symm_add_apply,       ← iterateFrobeniusEquiv_def, RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
PerfectRing.lift.description: A ring homomorphism from one characteristic p ring to another is constructed when the first is p-radical and the second is a perfect ring, leveraging given homomorphisms from a common source ring.

PerfectRing.lift_apply.code:
PerfectRing.lift_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p]
  [IsPRadical i p] (x : L) (n : ℕ) (y : K) (h : i y = x ^ p ^ n) :
  (lift i j p) x = (iterateFrobeniusEquiv M p n).symm (j y)

explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

PerfectRing.lift_apply.description: The application of a lifting process for homomorphisms between commutative rings allows the transformation of elements based on the relationship between a power of an element in one ring and its image in another through the Frobenius endomorphism.

PerfectRing.lift_comp_apply.code:
PerfectRing.lift_comp_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p]
  [IsPRadical i p] (x : K) : (lift i j p) (i x) = j x
PerfectRing.lift_comp_apply.description: The lifting operation applied to an image of an element under a ring homomorphism will equal the image of that element under a second homomorphism when the codomain is a perfect ring and both homomorphisms are compatible with a specific exponential characteristic.

IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_perfect.code:
IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_perfect.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} (M : Type u_3) [CommRing K]
  [CommRing L] [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar M p] [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing M p] :
  Function.Injective fun f => f.comp i
IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_perfect.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` is `p`-radical, then for any perfect ring `M` of exponential charactistic `p`,
the map `(L →+* M) → (K →+* M)` induced by `i` is injective.
A special case of `IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_pNilradical_eq_bot`.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.

IsPRadical.injective_comp_of_perfect.description: The composition of a p-radical homomorphism from one commutative ring to another preserves injectivity when mapping to a perfect ring of the same exponential characteristic.

PerfectRing.lift_comp.code:
PerfectRing.lift_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p]
  [IsPRadical i p] : (lift i j p).comp i = j

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.

PerfectRing.lift_comp.description: The composition of a lift of a p-radical homomorphism with itself results in another homomorphism to a ring of the same exponential characteristic.

PerfectRing.comp_lift.code:
PerfectRing.comp_lift.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (f : L →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p]
  [IsPRadical i p] : lift i (f.comp i) p = f

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.PerfectRing.lift: A ring homomorphism from one characteristic p ring to another is constructed when the first is p-radical and the second is a perfect ring, leveraging given homomorphisms from a common source ring.

PerfectRing.comp_lift.description: The lifting of a homomorphism composed with another homomorphism in the context of characteristic p rings equals the original homomorphism, when the first homomorphism preserves a p-radical structure and the target is a perfect ring.

PerfectRing.liftEquiv.code:
PerfectRing.liftEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} (M : Type u_3) [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] :
  (K →+* M) ≃ (L →+* M)
PerfectRing.liftEquiv.comment:
If `i : K →+* L` is a homomorphisms of characteristic `p` rings, such that
`i` is `p`-radical, and `M` is a perfect ring of characteristic `p`,
then `K →+* M` is one-to-one correspondence to
`L →+* M`, given by `PerfectRing.lift`. This is a generalization to `PerfectClosure.lift`.

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.PerfectRing.lift_comp: The composition of a lift of a p-radical homomorphism with itself results in another homomorphism to a ring of the same exponential characteristic.
explanatories.PerfectRing.comp_lift: The lifting of a homomorphism composed with another homomorphism in the context of characteristic p rings equals the original homomorphism, when the first homomorphism preserves a p-radical structure and the target is a perfect ring.
explanatories.OneHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a one homomorphism between two types that each have a one element.

PerfectRing.liftEquiv.fullDefinition: def liftEquiv : (K →+* M) ≃ (L →+* M) where   toFun j := lift i j p   invFun f := f.comp i   left_inv f := lift_comp i f p   right_inv f := comp_lift i f p
PerfectRing.liftEquiv.description: There is a one-to-one correspondence between homomorphisms from a commutative ring of characteristic p to a perfect ring of characteristic p, when the first ring's homomorphism is p-radical.

PerfectRing.lift_id.code:
PerfectRing.lift_id.{u_1, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing M] (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ)
  [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] : lift (RingHom.id K) j p = j

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.

PerfectRing.lift_id.description: Applying the lifting process from a trivial homomorphism on a characteristic p ring to another characteristic p ring yields the original homomorphism itself.

PerfectRing.liftEquiv_id_apply.code:
PerfectRing.liftEquiv_id_apply.{u_1, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing M] (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ)
  [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing M p] : (liftEquiv M (RingHom.id K) p) j = j

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.

PerfectRing.liftEquiv_id_apply.description: The application of the equivalence between the lifting and the identity homomorphism in characteristic p rings results in the original homomorphism.

PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift.code:
PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4} [CommRing K]
  [CommRing L] [CommRing M] [CommRing N] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (k : K →+* N) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p]
  [ExpChar M p] [ExpChar N p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing N p] [IsPRadical j p] :
  (lift j k p).comp (lift i j p) = lift i k p

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.

PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift.description: The composition of two lift maps in the context of perfect rings and exponential characteristic equals a single lift map when certain ideal and ring properties hold.

PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply.code:
PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4}
  [CommRing K] [CommRing L] [CommRing M] [CommRing N] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (k : K →+* N) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p]
  [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [ExpChar N p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing N p] [IsPRadical j p]
  (x : L) : (lift j k p) ((lift i j p) x) = (lift i k p) x
PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply.description: The composition of lifting homomorphisms applied to an element in one perfect ring leads to an equivalent lifting directly to another perfect ring under specified conditions.

PerfectRing.lift_self_apply.code:
PerfectRing.lift_self_apply.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommRing K] [CommRing L] (i : K →+* L) (p : ℕ)
  [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [IsPRadical i p] [PerfectRing L p] (x : L) : (lift i i p) x = x
PerfectRing.lift_self_apply.description: The lifting operation for a p-radical homomorphism on perfect rings acts as the identity on elements of the codomain.

PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply_eq_self.code:
PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply_eq_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K]
  [CommRing L] [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p]
  [PerfectRing M p] [IsPRadical i p] [IsPRadical j p] [PerfectRing L p] (x : L) : (lift j i p) ((lift i j p) x) = x
PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply_eq_self.description: The application of a lifting operation followed by another lifting operation to an element in a perfect ring results in the original element when both lifted homomorphisms are p-radical and the rings involved have the same exponential characteristic.

PerfectRing.lift_lift.code:
PerfectRing.lift_lift.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4} [CommRing K]
  [CommRing L] [CommRing M] [CommRing N] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (g : L →+* N) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p]

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.

PerfectRing.lift_lift.description: The lifting of a composition of two ring homomorphisms can be expressed as the lifting of the first homomorphism followed by the second, provided certain conditions related to exponential characteristic and p-radical properties are satisfied.

PerfectRing.liftEquiv_comp_apply.description: The composition of two p-radical-preserving homomorphisms followed by a lift to another commutative ring results in the same element as lifting first and then composing with the second homomorphism, provided all involved rings have exponential characteristic p and one of them is perfect.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]

IsPerfectClosure.equiv.comment:
If `L` and `M` are both perfect closures of `K`, then there is a ring isomorphism `L ≃+* M`.
This is similar to `IsAlgClosure.equiv` and `IsSepClosure.equiv`.

explanatories.PerfectRing.liftAux: A map can be constructed from elements in one commutative semiring to another, under the conditions that the source and target semirings are of characteristic p, the source homomorphism is p-radical, and the target semiring is a perfect ring, allowing for transition of elements based upon power roots.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv.fullDefinition: def equiv : L ≃+* M where   __ := PerfectRing.lift i j p   invFun := PerfectRing.liftAux j i p   left_inv := PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply_eq_self i j p   right_inv := PerfectRing.lift_comp_lift_apply_eq_self j i p
IsPerfectClosure.equiv.description: If two rings are both perfect closures of a given ring with the same exponential characteristic, then there exists a ring isomorphism between them.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_symm.code:

explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_symm.description: The inverse of the isomorphism between two perfect closures of a given ring with the same exponential characteristic is itself an isomorphism, demonstrating symmetry in the relationship.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_apply.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing L p]

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_apply.description: Given a perfect closure and the exponential characteristic of the involved rings, if an element in one ring can be expressed as a specific power of another element in a different ring, then the equivalence between the two homomorphisms applied to that element relates to the iteration of the Frobenius endomorphism applied to the image of the original element in the second ring.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_self_apply.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_self_apply.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [CommRing K] [CommRing L] (i : K →+* L)
  (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [PerfectRing L p] [IsPerfectClosure i p] (x : L) : (equiv i i p) x = x
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_self_apply.description: The application of the self-equivalence of a perfect closure for a homomorphism between commutative rings confirms that elements remain unchanged under this equivalence when the characteristic is a specified prime.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_apply.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing K] [CommRing L]
  [CommRing M] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p] [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [PerfectRing L p]
  [IsPerfectClosure i p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPerfectClosure j p] (x : K) : (equiv i j p) (i x) = j x
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_apply.description: The composition of two homomorphisms between perfect rings preserves the values when applying the equivalence between the homomorphisms on elements from the source ring.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4}
  [CommRing K] [CommRing L] [CommRing M] [CommRing N] (i : K →+* L) (j : K →+* M) (k : K →+* N) (p : ℕ) [ExpChar K p]
  [ExpChar L p] [ExpChar M p] [ExpChar N p] [PerfectRing L p] [IsPerfectClosure i p] [PerfectRing M p]
  [IsPerfectClosure j p] [PerfectRing N p] [IsPerfectClosure k p] (x : L) :
  (equiv j k p) ((equiv i j p) x) = (equiv i k p) x
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply.description: The composition of equivalences between perfect closures of homomorphisms in characteristic p rings is associative, meaning that applying one equivalence after another yields the same result as directly applying the equivalence between the first and last homomorphisms.

IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply_.code:
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply_eq_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}

  [PerfectRing L p] [IsPerfectClosure i p] [PerfectRing M p] [IsPerfectClosure j p] (x : L) :
  (equiv j i p) ((equiv i j p) x) = x
IsPerfectClosure.equiv_comp_equiv_apply_.description: The process of applying two successive equivalences between homomorphisms of perfect rings with a fixed characteristic results in the original element being unchanged.
